title: Fantrax STALE_CLIENT outage: API version 181.0.0 -> 185.1.0 (all Fantrax jobs down since 2026-08-01T13:01Z)
description:
All Fantrax-dependent scheduled jobs have failed continuously since 2026-08-01T13:01:00Z. Evidence from the run ledger (1249 records synced from s3://infrastack-statebucket446e0578-rm3scvdxnnyg/runledger/):

- 65 FAILED records total; 100% classify as STALE_CLIENT. No other failure mode present.
- Current episode: 2026-08-01T13:01:00Z -> ongoing (53 failures). Last SUCCESS before onset: 2026-08-01T12:01:14Z (gs-check). So Fantrax deployed between 12:01 and 13:01 UTC on 2026-08-01.
- Prior episode: 2026-07-01T17:00:53Z -> 2026-07-02T03:00:55Z (12 failures), same cause, fixed by fork PR #6 (180.0.0 -> 181.0.0).
- Affected commands: optimize (41), shadow/waivers/grade/transactions/claims/team-values (3 each), prospects/gs-check (2 each), recap-site/backtest (1 each).
- Only survivors are 'archive' and 'projection-site' — the two commands that need no Fantrax auth.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED BY CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT, not inference. Same POST to /fxpa/req getUserInfo, only the 'v' field differs:
  v=181.0.0 -> {"pageError":{"code":"STALE_CLIENT"}}
  v=185.1.0 -> {"data":{"sDate":...},"roles":["03"], pageError WARNING_NOT_LOGGED_IN}
The 185.1.0 response passes the version gate; WARNING_NOT_LOGGED_IN is expected since the probe carried no auth cookie.

Current version discovered from the Fantrax Angular bundle's embedded package.json (chunk-3DDNW3YR.js): {name:'fantrax',version:'185.1.0'}.

Two pin sites must move together:
1. fork github.com/nixon-commits/go-fantrax auth_client/fantrax_client.go:40 const fantraxAPIVersion
2. rosterbot internal/fantrax/gs_check.go:56 "v" literal (builds its own /fxpa/req payload)
acceptance_criteria: Both pin sites at 185.1.0; rosterbot go.mod replace bumped to the new fork commit; a live non-dry-run Fantrax command succeeds locally; scheduled jobs return to SUCCESS in the run ledger.
close_reason: Fixed + verified. Fantrax 181.0.0 -> 185.1.0 both pin sites (fork 5b9d97f + gs_check.go). Merged 385529d, image d9af8629. Production recovery CONFIRMED: 2026-08-03T17:01:36Z optimize = SUCCESS, ending a 53-failure streak that ran from 2026-08-01T13:01Z.

title: Lineup-apply loop resolved --matchup dates to the weekly Scoring Period number, not the daily period, causing duplicate Pushover storms
description:
internal/lineuprun.go's per-date apply loop (used by both optimize and shadow via internal/lineuprun.Run) resolved each --dates/--matchup date to a Fantrax scoring period via fantrax.ResolvePeriod(periods, currentPeriod, seasonStart, today, date), introduced by rosterbot-z3b (2026-07-12). ResolvePeriod's tier 1 trusts periods (from GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams) as an authoritative per-DAY period map, but that list is actually the weekly matchup 'Scoring Period' schedule (~7 days/period, wider around breaks). Since virtually every in-season date falls inside some weekly period's date range, tier 1 won on nearly every call, overriding the correct daily anchor arithmetic (tiers 2/3).

Discovered 2026-07-14 investigating user report of repeated duplicate Pushover lineup-change notifications. The All-Star break merged two weeks into weekly period 16 (2026-07-13..07-26). Every hourly Lineup Fargate run (12x/day, optimize --matchup) evaluated --matchup dates 2026-07-16 through 2026-07-26 (11 distinct calendar dates), and ALL of them resolved to period 16 via ResolvePeriod tier 1. Confirmed via CloudWatch logs (log group InfraStack-Logs6819BB44-evRuHY7lXtHK): GetHitterRosterForPeriod(16)/GetPitcherRosterForPeriod(16) fetched the identical stale snapshot for all 11 dates, ApplyLineup(16, ...) wrote all 11 dates' changes to the same period, and because each date's real target-day diff never converged, the identical lineup swap (same players, same +25.93 pts, same 'locked players -- retrying without 9 player(s)' apply-rejection) re-applied and re-fired a Pushover notification for all 11 dates on every single hourly run -- 11 duplicate notifications/hour, hour after hour.

This is the same architectural flaw as rosterbot-uv6 (GetTeamGS's daily walk mistakenly routed through the same periods-list-first resolver), which was fixed for that one call site via gsPeriodWalk/dailyPeriodFor bypassing ResolvePeriod entirely. rosterbot-z3b's consolidation reintroduced the identical mistake one call site later (the apply loop) without recognizing the periods list was weekly, not daily -- its own scoping notes assumed GS-budget/gscheck 'agree with ResolvePeriod's tier 1 by construction' without checking whether the apply loop's needs matched tier 1's actual data shape.
design: Fixed by: (1) exporting fantrax.dailyPeriodFor as fantrax.DailyPeriodFor (gs_period_walk.go) as the single source for date-to-daily-period resolution; (2) switching internal/lineuprun.go's apply loop to call DailyPeriodFor directly instead of ResolvePeriod; (3) deleting fantrax.ResolvePeriod and its test file entirely (period_resolver.go/period_resolver_test.go) -- with the apply loop fixed, it had zero remaining production callers, and no safe production use case exists for it: every real caller needs the daily axis, which the weekly periods list structurally cannot provide. FindCurrentPeriod (still used directly by the GS-limit lookup, which correctly wants the weekly number) and DailyPeriodFor now cleanly own their respective axes with no shared resolver conflating them. CLAUDE.md's Fantrax section rewritten to document the two-axis distinction explicitly so a future consolidation doesn't repeat this.
acceptance_criteria: go build/vet/test clean across the repo. TestGSPeriodWalk_MergedAllStarBreakDailyNumbering and TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod (existing regression coverage for the two axes) still pass. Manually verified DailyPeriodFor resolves 2026-07-16..07-26 (today=2026-07-14) to 11 distinct daily periods (114..124), not a collapsed 16. Next deployed hourly Lineup run should show each --matchup date fetching/applying against its own distinct period and converging to 'No changes needed' on subsequent runs instead of re-notifying every hour.
notes: Relates to rosterbot-uv6/rosterbot-wd5 (same bug class, different call site) and rosterbot-uw6 (deferred validation of daily-period numbering across this same ASB merge window, for the GS-tally axis -- still relevant, unaffected by this fix). Not yet deployed as of filing -- fix is committed locally; deploy via push to main (CodeBuild) picks it up on the next scheduled Lineup task launch.
close_reason: fantrax.DailyPeriodFor wired into internal/lineuprun.go's apply loop; fantrax.ResolvePeriod deleted (zero remaining safe callers). Build/vet/test clean; verified 11 distinct daily periods for the merged-ASB date range that previously collapsed to one. Committed, pending push/deploy.

title: Fix rotted chromium pin in Dockerfile blocking all CodeBuild deploys
description: CodeBuild (image build on push to main) has been FAILED since ~07:03 PDT 2026-07-12 (builds 71-75). Root cause: Dockerfile:34 pins chromium=147.0.7727.137-1~deb12u1 exactly, and Debian dropped that point release from the live bookworm repo -> 'Version not found' (apt exit 100) -> docker build fails -> no image pushed -> in-build cdk deploy never runs -> blocks ALL infra+image changes (incl. the rosterbot-00j BuildNotify rule/lambda, which therefore don't exist and never notify). Fix: bump ARG CHROMIUM_VERSION to current bookworm main (150.0.7871.100-1~deb12u1, arm64 confirmed) and CI-validate on Graviton via the existing headless smoke test. Note: 150.0.7871.46 previously SIGTRAP'd on Graviton; .100 is a newer point release under validation.
close_reason: Shipped: #42 (chromium 150.0.7871.100, builds 76/77 green) + #41 (BuildNotify rule live, notifications firing). Re-closing on main dolt branch.

title: Move WebAuthn credentials onto UserStore + enrollment redemption for login
description:
rosterbot-crq.10 delivered per-caller AUTHORIZATION but left AUTHENTICATION single-tenant. Passkey credentials still live on the singleton Identity record (webauthn/identity.json), not in the UserStore, so UserStore.Credentials/PutCredential/DeleteCredential/UserByCredential are implemented, conformance-tested, and NOT on the live path.

Consequence today: exactly one person can log in with a passkey. ensureUserForIdentity creates a tenant record for that person so authorization resolves, but a second user has nowhere to register a credential.

What this needs:

1. register/begin + register/finish take their user from a REDEEMED ENROLLMENT rather than from loadOrCreateIdentity. The enrollment primitive and store already exist (rosterbot-crq.9); nothing consumes them yet. Redemption is single-use and atomic, so the ceremony must redeem at FINISH, not at begin -- redeeming at begin burns the link on an abandoned ceremony and the user cannot retry.

2. login/begin + login/finish resolve the user from the discoverable credential's user handle, which IS the UserID (see lineupapi.UserID). BeginLogin currently takes the singleton; it needs the per-user credential list. The non-discoverable fallback goes through UserByCredential.

3. Sign-counter updates write one credential key (PutCredential), not the whole record -- that is the contention-free property the key layout was designed for.

4. Session mint uses the resolved user's real TokenVersion instead of the hardcoded 0.

5. canRegister's global bootstrap token stops authorizing enrollment (rosterbot-crq.9 filed this; crq.10 did not remove it). The token stays an admin break-glass for the API, but must no longer enroll a passkey against an arbitrary identity.

6. A one-time migration of the singleton's credentials into the UserStore, or a read-through that prefers UserStore and falls back to Identity during cutover. migrate-identity already copies them; decide whether the handler reads UserStore only (requires the migration to have run) or both.

VERIFY WITH TWO REAL USERS. Chrome virtual authenticators via CDP make this testable headlessly -- rosterbot-crq.10 used the technique against a live . The test that matters is two distinct authenticators, two enrollments, and each user seeing only their own session; a single-user test cannot distinguish working multi-tenancy from the current state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two users can each enroll a passkey via their own single-use enrollment link and log in independently.
- An enrollment link is spent only on a COMPLETED registration; an abandoned ceremony leaves it usable.
- Login resolves the user from the credential, not from a singleton, and the minted session carries that user's real TokenVersion.
- Revoking a credential removes it from both the user's credential set and the lookup index.
- The bootstrap token can no longer enroll a passkey.
- Verified with two distinct virtual authenticators, not one.

title: Lineup delta credits already-active slot changes as full activations
description:
combinedMovesDelta (internal/lineuprun/display.go:30) credits the FULL projected points of every entry in `activate`, debiting only entries in `bench`. Both optimizer paths emit already-active players into ToActivate whenever only their SLOT changed (internal/optimizer/lineup.go:84, internal/optimizer/pitcher_lineup.go:159: `if currentAssign[ps.PlayerID] != ps.PosID`). Such a player never appears in `bench`, so nothing cancels the credit and his full pts are counted as phantom gain.

Live case, `optimize --dry-run --no-cache --dates 2026-08-14`:
    Changes (+5.28 pts)
      up Sam Antonacci -> 3B  +5.24
      up Jake Bauers   -> OF  +4.32
      dn Angel Genao   -> BN  -4.28
Antonacci was already active at OF (the table's Slot column renders sp.Player.RosterPosition, i.e. current Fantrax state, display.go:263). True net gain = Bauers - Genao = +0.04. Reported +5.28. Inflation = +5.24, exactly Antonacci's pts.

Reproduced directly against combinedMovesDelta:
  - live case: reported +5.28, true +0.04
  - PURE slot shuffle (a: OF->UT, b: UT->OF, nobody enters or leaves): reported +8.00, true 0.00, isZeroGainDelta = FALSE

Production corroboration (CloudWatch InfraStack-Logs6819BB44-evRuHY7lXtHK, 3d), activations vs benchings per run stream: d51c2047 9v6, c8cb9bb0 8v5, 2d1d5164 8v6, 97be570b 6v5, a043a0f1 3v1. Corroborating only, not proof on its own -- an activation into a genuinely empty slot also needs no pairing. The 11-day delta distribution is bimodal: either <0.5 or clustered at ~4.5 / ~9 / ~13.5 / ~23, i.e. multiples of one hitter's projected pts.

CONSEQUENCES
1. The movesZeroGain gate (emit.go:171, display.go:25) is a no-op for pure slot shuffles. That gate exists because Fantrax rejects a payload ATOMICALLY if any player in it is per-player-locked -- the Apr 26 incident pinned at display_test.go:103. It only covers swaps where activated players came off the bench; the common case is uncovered, so valueless payloads still reach the live roster. (No apply failures in the last 11 days, so the risk has not yet materialised.)
2. The primary user-facing decision metric -- the Changes line and the Pushover body -- is inflated.
3. Likely root cause of rosterbot-cem.

NOT a lineup-selection bug: optimalAssignment (lineup.go:70) is correct and independent of the delta. Valuation and gating only.
design:
Make the delta measure change in ACTIVE MEMBERSHIP, not change in slot assignment.

(a) Thread currentAssign (or a currently-active player-ID set) into combinedMovesDelta and skip the credit for any activate entry whose player was already active; or
(b) have the optimizer return slot-only moves in a field separate from true activations.

(a) is smaller and preserves the emit-only-changes behaviour. Note the APPLY payload still needs the slot-change entries -- Fantrax must be told the new slot. Only the VALUATION may ignore them. Do not change which lineup is chosen.

Interaction with rosterbot-cem: cem proposes a min-gain threshold of ~1.0-1.5 pts to damp churn. That will NOT suppress these moves -- a phantom shuffle reports ~4.5-9 pts and clears any such threshold comfortably. This bead should land first or cem will not meet its acceptance criteria.

Tests: extend TestCombinedMovesDelta (display_test.go:96) with (1) an already-active slot-changer alongside a genuine swap, expecting only the genuine net; (2) a pure slot shuffle expecting 0.0 and isZeroGainDelta == true. Add the pitcher-path equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: Reported delta equals genuine net gain (slot-only moves contribute 0); a pure slot shuffle is classified movesZeroGain and is not submitted; regression tests cover both the hitter and pitcher paths; go test ./internal/lineuprun/... ./internal/optimizer/... passes; optimize --dry-run on the 2026-08-14 roster state reports +0.04 rather than +5.28.

comments.author: Jon Nixon
comments.text:
BEFORE-FIX BASELINE, for measuring this change's effect (2026-08-14 audit).

Lineup gap vs hindsight-optimal:
  2026-07-27..08-02   actual 742  optimal 977  gap -235  efficiency 76.0%
  2026-08-03..08-09   actual 590  optimal 814  gap -224  efficiency 72.5%

Note the gap is structural, not a symptom of this bug -- 'optimal' is hindsight-optimal and with MAE ~5.4 FP/game no projection-driven lineup closes it. Fixing this bead should NOT be expected to move the gap much, because optimalAssignment already picks the right lineup; the defect is in valuation and gating. What it SHOULD move is churn (rosterbot-cem: 64% no-op runs, 75% re-flips) and the volume of pointless writes to the live roster.

Stated explicitly so the fix is not judged against the wrong metric. If the gap does improve materially, that would be a surprise worth investigating on its own.

Also worth knowing: no apply failures appear in CloudWatch over the 11 days before this audit, so the atomic-rejection risk this bug exposes has not yet been realised in production -- the fix is preventive, not a response to active breakage.

title: HKB name join is last-write-wins on collision; four live namesake pairs
description:
internal/lineuprun/hkbmeta.go builds its lookup as:

  out[playername.Normalize(p.Name)] = lineupapi.Dynasty{Age: p.Age, Value: p.Value}

The assignment is unconditional, so when two HKB players normalize to the same
key the LAST one in range order wins. Range order over the scraped slice is
stable-ish but arbitrary, and nothing records that a choice was made.

MEASURED against the live HKB rankings on 2026-08-13 (1752 players, 1748
distinct normalized keys) — four colliding keys:

  luis garcia    Luis García Jr. (NYY, MLB,         age 26.2, value 1139)
                 Luis Garcia     (NYY, ROOKIE_BALL, age 29.7, value 10)
  max muncy      Max Muncy       (ATH, MLB,         age 23.9, value 385)
                 Max Muncy       (LAD, MLB,         age 35.9, value 346)
  fernando cruz  Fernando Cruz   (NYY, MLB,         age 36.4, value 27)
                 Fernando Cruz   (CHC, LOW_A,       age 19.7, value 10)
  wilmer flores  Wilmer Flores   (FA,  MLB,         age 35.0, value 10)
                 Wilmer Flores   (DET, LOW_A,       age 25.5, value 10)

WHY IT MATTERS
The wire fields are omitempty and a MISS renders as unknown — that path is
well handled and documented. A WRONG MATCH does not: it renders as a
confident, plausible number. Roster a player on a colliding key and the
lineup page can show a 1139-value MLB regular as value 10 / age 29.7, and
nothing in the UI, the JSON or the logs distinguishes that from the truth.

This is the failure class CLAUDE.md already documents one level down for
MLBAM ids (`claimName`, the retired-namesake bug where last-write-wins
produced confidently wrong data rather than a visible failure). The same
shape has now reappeared on the HKB join.

`luis garcia` is the sharpest case: Normalize strips BOTH the diacritic in
"García" and the "Jr." suffix, so the normalization that makes the join work
is exactly what creates the collision. This one is in principle fixable.
`max muncy` is two genuinely active MLB players and is NOT fixable by any
string transformation — same as the two-Will-Smiths case CLAUDE.md notes.

CURRENT EXPOSURE
Latent, not live. Verified on 2026-08-13: all 36 players in the published
lineup resolve to a real HKB row and none sits on a colliding key. It bites
whenever one of these eight players (or a future namesake pair) is rostered.

NOTE the blast radius is wider than the lineup page. playername.Normalize is
the HKB join key for internal/claims, internal/transactions and
internal/teamvalue too. teamvalue feeds the durable Team Value Store, which
is NoBackfill (docs/adr/0002) — a wrong value there is not re-derivable.
Worth checking whether those call sites have the same unconditional-assign
shape before deciding the fix.

REPRODUCTION
Committed as a diag-tagged harness (never runs in CI):

  go test -tags diag -run TestDiagHKBJoin -v ./internal/lineuprun/

It reports every colliding key with both rows, and asserts that each
published age/value round-trips to a real HKB row.

POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS (not yet decided)
- Prefer the MLB-level row over a minor-league one on collision; that alone
  resolves luis garcia, fernando cruz and wilmer flores, and is a real signal
  HKB already gives us (Level / Prospect fields).
- Detect collisions and refuse to guess — leave the key absent so it renders
  as unknown rather than as another player's number. Consistent with how
  tradevalue withholds a verdict when its two methods disagree.
- Disambiguate with the Fantrax team/position we already hold at the lookup
  site, rather than at map-build time.
Whichever is chosen, the two-active-MLB-players case (max muncy) still needs
a defined behavior; "unknown" is defensible there.
design:
CONFIRMED REPO-WIDE, not lineup-specific.

internal/hkb/enrich.go:30 BuildLookup has the identical unconditional-assign
shape:

  func BuildLookup(players []Player) map[string]Player {
      m := make(map[string]Player, len(players))
      for _, p := range players {
          m[playername.Normalize(p.Name)] = p   // last-write-wins
      }
      return m
  }

Call sites of the SAME defect:
  internal/teamvalue/aggregate.go:36   -> Team Value Store (NoBackfill,
                                          docs/adr/0002 — a wrong value here
                                          is NOT re-derivable later)
  internal/tradeboard/tradeboard.go:135 -> league values table
  internal/tradeboard/tradeboard.go:193 -> (second build)
  internal/hkb/enrich.go:42 Enrich      -> claims / transactions enrichment

And internal/lineuprun/hkbmeta.go:41 hkbMeta re-implements the same loop
independently rather than calling BuildLookup — so the bug is written twice.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX
The right home is hkb.BuildLookup: fixing it once covers teamvalue,
tradeboard, claims and transactions together. hkbMeta should then be
rewritten in terms of it (or of whatever collision-aware type replaces it)
instead of keeping its own copy — a second copy of the keying is how the two
would drift apart again.

Note the severity is not uniform across those call sites. The lineup page
renders a wrong number for one day and self-corrects tomorrow; the Team Value
Store PERSISTS it forever, and trade valuations turn it into a decision. That
argues for the conservative option (refuse to guess on a collision) at least
for the durable and decision-making paths.

title: P4: per-tenant job fan-out
description:
Cron -> Lambda enumerates active tenants -> N RunTask, each with one tenant's TEAM_ID and RUN_USER_ID.

One ECS task per user per job is FORCED, not chosen: auth_client.Client is {http.Client, LeagueID, UseCache} with no credential field, and every request calls a package-global GetCookies(). Two tenants cannot coexist in one process without forking go-fantrax.

Only ~7 of 15 schedules fan out - Lineup (hourly), Grade, Backtest, Shadow, Prospects, ProjectionSite. The rest are league-wide singletons. The expensive rate-limited upstreams (FanGraphs, Savant, HKB, MLB) are all on the singleton side, so fan-out multiplies cheap work only - and avoids becoming 12x the load on FanGraphs, which would get an IP blocked and take down every tenant at once.

- Run ledger, progress and notifications all become per-tenant.
- Tenants excluded from fan-out by status, so a parked account costs nothing.
- propose-only is the default; only tenants with auto_apply=true reach ApplyLineup.
- rosterbot-crq.1 already re-keyed opsalert by (command, user_id) - verify it actually discriminates once real tenant ids appear, since it has never run against a non-empty user_id.

Cost at 12 tenants is ~$8.60/mo Fargate. The 2 GB task exists for chromedp, which now measurably runs about once a year - a smaller task def for non-connect work roughly halves it.

title: P3: Fantrax connect task + credential ladder + per-tenant session isolation
description:
The server half of the connect flow (rosterbot-crq.5 is the UI half).

Flow: browser POSTs Fantrax creds to the API Lambda -> Lambda encrypts under the CMK with EncryptionContext{user_id} (it holds kms:Encrypt only) -> writes ciphertext -> launches a connect ECS task -> task decrypts (only role that can), drives chromedp, captures FX_RM, writes it back encrypted, sets conn_status. Browser polls GET /v1/runs/{id}/progress, which already exists.

The password must never enter an ECS task override (CloudTrail logs those) nor any log line. Request-body logging stays off. KMS records the encryption context, not the plaintext - that context is the audit trail of whose credential was read, by what, when.

Ownership proof at connect, failing closed:
  invite.team_id in TeamRosterResponse.MyTeamIDs   hard fail
  TEAM#<team_id> unclaimed (conditional write)     hard fail
  UserInfo.Email == invite.email                   WARN only - a manager may
                                                   legitimately use a different
                                                   address with Fantrax

LADDER, and the no-retry rule is load-bearing:
  FX_RM -> 401 -> re-login with stored creds -> failure ->
    conn_status = needs_reconnect
    STOP all applies for that tenant (fail safe, not fail open)
    in-app banner + admin alert
    DO NOT RETRY until the user reconnects

FX_RM rejected means the session aged out; re-login is correct. Re-login rejected means the password is wrong, and retrying is actively harmful - repeated failed logins trigger account lockout and Cloudflare bot-blocking, so an hourly retry across 14 runs/day would lock a pilot out of their own Fantrax account using credentials they gave us.

Emit a distinct login_challenge_or_timeout error class when the flow completes without yielding FX_RM, so a 2FA-enabled user is diagnosable rather than a mystery. Keep the devtools-paste path as a seam even if unsurfaced.

title: P2: tenant-scoped S3 state (user=<uid>/ Hive segment) + backfill
description:
Per-tenant artifacts get a Hive segment right after the artifact prefix: analysis/grades/user=U/dt=D/system=S/.

internal/s3blob makes this nearly free: its contract is that every key is RELATIVE to the prefix (joined in, stripped out), so a per-tenant store is a Blob built with a longer prefix. statestore composes it; s3blob and every key parser (the Analysis Store's system= segment, the ledger's inverted timestamps) are untouched.

- layout.Artifact gains PerTenant bool. Per-tenant: Backtest, Analysis, LineupGaps, Lineup, RunLedger, RunOutput, Progress, Notification, Trades, TradeOffers, Reports, Session. Shared: Cache (keys already carry teamID), TeamValues, Archive, Claims, TradeValues, FootballValues.
- Athena partition projection gains user.
- Backfill existing state to user=<jon-uid>/.
- The Infra page's gap scan must iterate per tenant.

SESSION/ IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. auth_client.CacheFile is a package CONST, so every tenant's task writes the same local path - correct only because each task is its own container. If two tenants ever share the session/ prefix, tenant B authenticates AS tenant A. That is a wrong-roster-write, not a data leak.

GATE: byte-identical --dry-run output vs a binary built from the last good commit, per CLAUDE.md's internal/lineuprun verification note (identical stream redirection, back-to-back runs). A correct tenancy refactor is output-preserving at N=1. This oracle disappears the moment a second tenant exists.
close_reason: Layout dimension, statestore composition, production backfill (3767 objects verified), Athena user partition, and per-tenant Infra health. Nothing sets a tenant yet — that flip is crq.13.

title: P1: route authorization - tenant-scoped vs admin-only
description:
Every /v1/* route today is isAuthed = any valid session OR the bearer token (handler.go:106). Correct for one operator; a flat 'every user sees everything' at N>1.

Split into three classes:
  TENANT-SCOPED  lineup, runs, run output/progress, notifications, trades, trades/values,
                 reports/*, passkeys - filtered to the caller's uid
  ADMIN-ONLY     infra (reveals the whole bucket layout and health), user management,
                 enrollment-link minting, league-wide job triggers
  SHARED         the already-public league views (recap site, value.json, football.json)

POST /v1/jobs/{name} needs care: a tenant may trigger jobs for their OWN tenant (re-optimize now), never league-wide ones (archive, recap-site, version-check), and it spends real AWS money so it needs a per-tenant rate limit.

Decision 12 is strict isolation - tenants are competitors in one league, so a leak of trade valuations or lineup intent is a game-integrity problem, not just privacy. Decision 13 grants admin read of everything, DISCLOSED at signup.

The bearer token becomes an admin credential, not a tenant one. It must not resolve to a uid.

title: P1: enrollment links - one primitive for invite and recovery
description:
An invite and a recovery are the same thing: a single-use, short-TTL, user-scoped token authorizing exactly one passkey enrollment. Build it once.

  ENROLL#<sha256(token)>  TOKEN  uid, team_id, email, expires_at (DDB TTL), used_at

Store the HASH, never the token. Admin-only mint endpoint. Redeeming authorizes register/begin+finish for THAT uid only, then burns (conditional write on used_at).

This REPLACES canRegister's current global bootstrap token for user enrollment (webauthn.go:77). That token grants enrollment against an identity model with no notion of whose - harmless at N=1, a god token at N>1. Keep the bearer token as an admin break-glass for the API, but it must no longer be a way to enroll a passkey against an arbitrary user.

The invite carries team_id because the connect flow proves ownership against it (see the Fantrax connect issue). Minting is where you assert 'Dave owns team 7'; connect is where Fantrax confirms it.
close_reason: Primitive, both stores, conformance suite, and the invite CLI. HTTP redeem endpoint lands with crq.10.

title: P1: User + credential model on DynamoDB, migrate the singleton Identity
description:
Replace the single-operator Identity (identity.go:18 'There is exactly one Identity for the whole dashboard') with per-user records.

Schema (design doc has the full table):
  USER#<uid>  PROFILE           display_name, email, role, status, auto_apply=false, token_version
  USER#<uid>  CRED#<cred_id>    public_key, sign_count, aaguid, transports, last_used_at
  CRED#<cred_id> USER           uid            (non-discoverable fallback lookup)
  EMAIL#<lower>  USER           uid            (uniqueness, conditional write)
  TEAM#<team_id> USER           uid            (one claimant per team)

uid IS the WebAuthn user handle newWebAuthnUserID() already mints. Because the code requires discoverable credentials (ResidentKeyRequirementRequired), the authenticator returns that handle at login, so 'who is this' is a direct key-get with NO index. CRED# exists only for the non-discoverable path.

MUST run through internal/lineupapi/identitytest.Run - that conformance suite is the contract, because rosterbot-crq.2 made Version opaque and ride on the struct, so an implementation that ignores it still compiles. Conditional writes give the optimistic concurrency crq.2 established.

Migration: create Jon as user 1 from the existing webauthn/ identity record, preserving the existing WebAuthnUserID and every credential, so current passkeys keep working. A migration that invalidates the operator's own passkeys locks the dashboard.

ListActiveTenants is a Scan, deliberately - one request at this scale, cheaper than a GSI. Revisit at four digits.
close_reason: Model, conformance suite, file store, DynamoDB store, and migration. Not wired into handlers (crq.10).

title: P1: DynamoDB identity table + KMS CMK + split-role IAM (CDK)
description:
Infrastructure only. No consumers yet, nothing reads or writes it.

- One DynamoDB table, PK/SK strings, on-demand billing, TTL attribute enabled (expires_at) for ENROLL# items. Point-in-time recovery on: this is the only store in the tree whose loss cannot be regenerated from upstream.
- One KMS CMK for Fantrax credential envelope encryption.
- THE SPLIT IS THE POINT (decision 6): apiFn gets kms:Encrypt ONLY; the ECS task role gets kms:Decrypt ONLY. The API Lambda has a public Function URL (AuthType: NONE), so if it could decrypt, every auth bug in lineupapi would be a password-disclosure bug. Grant both DynamoDB read/write.
- Table name reaches consumers by env var, not a hardcoded string.

Do NOT deploy. Write the CDK; deployment is a separate approved step. Note infra.go's documented circular-dependency hazards around the dashboard distribution before adding any GetAtt.
close_reason: CDK written and synth-verified; not deployed

title: make run-all cannot fail: trailing echo discards every command's exit status
description:
CLAUDE.md calls 'make run-all' the canonical end-to-end smoke test and prescribes it as the sanity check before pushing changes. It cannot report failure.

Every recipe line has the shape:

    @echo "=== X ===";  time go run . X;  echo

In shell, 'a; b' exits with b's status. The trailing bare 'echo' therefore discards the exit code of every 'go run' in the target. Only two lines (backtest --recency-experiment, projection-site) carry an explicit '|| true', which makes the others read as though they are load-bearing. They are not - all of them are equally ignored.

Demonstrated live on 2026-08-12: a cold 'make clean-cache && make run-all' on merged main ran football-values and football-trades, both of which printed

    Error: football config: missing required env var: SLEEPER_LEAGUE_ID

and the target still exited 0.

This is the failure class rosterbot-00e was filed for, in CLAUDE.md's own words: 'a guard that silently no-ops is the false-confidence failure this one exists to kill.' A smoke test that always passes is worse than none, because it is trusted.

Note the fix must decide what to do about commands that legitimately cannot run locally (the two football ones need SLEEPER_LEAGUE_ID, which lives in SSM for prod). Options: an explicit skip-if-unset guard that reports SKIPPED, or keeping '|| true' on exactly those lines with a comment saying why - the point is that ignoring a failure becomes a visible, deliberate act rather than a side effect of formatting.
acceptance_criteria:
- A non-zero exit from any run-all command fails the target, except where a line explicitly and commentedly opts out.
- Commands that cannot run without local-only env (football-values, football-trades) either report SKIPPED or opt out explicitly with a stated reason.
- Verify by making one command fail on purpose and confirming 'make run-all' exits non-zero.
- CLAUDE.md's description of run-all stays accurate.

title: lambda/main.go never wires Trades/TradeValues -> /v1/trades returns 501 in production
description:
internal/lineupapi/handler.go routes GET /v1/trades and GET /v1/trades/values, gated behind cfg.Trades / cfg.TradeValues (ObjectStore). Both are nil in the Lambda: lambda/main.go never sets them in the lineupapi.Config literal.

Handler behavior when nil is 501 'not configured'. So both endpoints have returned 501 in production since the Trades tab shipped, and the dashboard's Trades tab cannot load.

infra.go ALREADY grants the IAM for the trades/ and tradevalues/ prefixes, so this is purely missing wiring at the composition root - the producers write, the storage is readable, nothing serves it.

Confirmed never wired on any branch: 'git log --all -S"Trades:" -- lambda/main.go' returns nothing.

cmd/serve.go (local) DOES wire them, which is why this never showed up in local dev.

Found in passing while implementing rosterbot-crq.3, which wires a sibling field (Reports) into the same Config literal correctly. Left unfixed deliberately: fixing it starts serving real data on live infrastructure, which is outside that ticket's scope and wants its own review.
acceptance_criteria:
- lambda/main.go builds Trades and TradeValues stores (s3lineup, keyed on the trades/ and tradevalues/ prefixes) and sets them on lineupapi.Config.
- A test at the composition root asserts the Config fields are non-nil, so the next field added here cannot silently repeat this.
- After deploy: authenticated GET /v1/trades returns 200 with the stored bytes, not 501.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed on claude/multiuser-passkey-auth-8ee4c9. Not yet merged to main, not deployed.

title: Move per-tenant dashboard artifacts off the world-readable report/ path
description:
report/* is world-readable through CloudFront's default behavior. CLAUDE.md records this explicitly as the reason the Trades tab was put on /v1/* instead: 'They are on /v1/* and therefore passkey-gated on purpose: report/* is world-readable through CloudFront's default behavior, and an open offer is not something to publish before deciding on it.'

Today report/ carries model.json, value.json, gap.json, views.json, written by cmd/projection-site.go and synced under DASHBOARD_BUCKET's report/ prefix.

Once these become per-tenant:
  gap.json   -> per-manager lineup efficiency. Publishing it tells the open internet how many points each manager leaves on their bench.
  model.json -> per-manager projection grades.
  value.json -> legitimately league-wide, stays.
  views.json -> recap readership, admin-ish, should not be public either.

The tenants are competitors in one league, so 'leaked to another tenant' is worse than 'leaked to a stranger' - this is a game-integrity issue, not just a privacy one.

Fixable today at N=1 and worth doing first: the current single-tenant gap.json is already Jon's own performance data sitting on an unauthenticated URL.
acceptance_criteria:
- gap.json, model.json and views.json are served from authenticated /v1/* endpoints (same passthrough contract as GET /v1/trades - stored bytes, untouched).
- value.json stays public.
- Dashboard SPA fetches the moved artifacts through the authenticated path.
- Verify: unauthenticated GET of the old report/ URLs 403/404s after cutover.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed on claude/multiuser-passkey-auth-8ee4c9. Not yet merged to main, not deployed.

title: opsalert: key Streak/Overdue by (command, user_id)
description:
internal/opsalert keys both of its decision functions on r.Command alone. Correct at N=1, silently wrong under per-tenant fan-out.

Streak (streak.go:102-105) filters 'r.Command != command' then walks newest-first, where a SUCCESS breaks the streak. With N tenants running the same command, tenant B failing EVERY hour returns verdict None, because other tenants' successes are interleaved in the same command's records.

Overdue (heartbeat.go:115) keeps newest[r.Command], so 'Lineup ran recently' is true if ANY tenant ran. A tenant whose task never launches is invisible permanently.

Overdue exists precisely because of rosterbot-ys8 - 'a job that never launches emits no event, writes no ledger record, and produces perfect silence, which is indistinguishable from perfect health'. Fan-out reintroduces that exact blindness one level down, and does so invisibly: code compiles, runs, reports green.

MUST land in or before the fan-out commit. Alerting that inverts is worse than no alerting.
acceptance_criteria:
- Streak and Overdue both key on (command, user_id); records with no user_id fall back to current behavior so single-tenant history still grades.
- Test: N tenants, one failing consecutively while others succeed -> Escalated fires for the failing tenant only.
- Test: N tenants, one absent entirely -> Overdue reports that tenant as missed while others are healthy.
- opsalert stays a stdlib-only leaf; opsalert.Record gains user_id and lineupapi/opsalert_contract_test.go is extended to guard the duplication.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed on claude/multiuser-passkey-auth-8ee4c9. Not yet merged to main, not deployed.

title: Multiuser tenancy with passkey auth
description:
Umbrella for making rosterbot multi-tenant: other managers in the league sign in with their own passkey and the bot manages their team.

Design settled by interview 2026-08-12. Full decision table, schema, sequencing and measured evidence in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-12-multiuser-passkey-tenancy-design.md.

Scope: pilot. One team per user, one league (the configured FANTRAX_LEAGUE_ID), small cohort of known managers, propose-only by default.

Phases:
  0. Latent bugs fixable today at N=1 (this epic's first three children)
  1. Identity substrate at N=1 (Dynamo, CMK, split IAM, session subject, enrollment links, route authz)
  2. Tenant state at N=1 (layout.PerTenant, statestore prefix composition, backfill, Athena user partition)
  3. Fantrax connection (connect form, ECS connect task, credential ladder, per-tenant session isolation)
  4. Fan-out (cron enumerates tenants, per-tenant ledger/progress/notifications, propose-only default)
  5. Pilot ops (admin Tenants tab, failure taxonomy routing, signup disclosure)

Gate on phases 1-2: byte-identical --dry-run output vs a binary built from the last good commit, per CLAUDE.md's internal/lineuprun verification note. A correct tenancy refactor is output-preserving at N=1. This oracle disappears once a second tenant exists.

title: [bug] ResolveMLBAMIDs silently resolves common names to the wrong player (namesake collision, last-write-wins)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

`playername.ResolveMLBAMIDs` silently resolves common names to the **wrong
player** — not a missing ID, a confidently wrong one. Found while diagnosing
`rosterbot-i52` on 2026-08-11 by cross-checking the resolver against Sleeper's
MLB player table over a 133-name Fantrax set.

## Measured, and verified against statsapi itself

| Fantrax name | resolver returned | who that actually is | correct ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jose Altuve | 501447 | Jose Altuve, **C, b.1988, inactive** | **514888** (2B, b.1990, active) |
| Jose Ramirez | 691342 | José Ramírez, **P, b.2003, inactive** | **608070** (3B, b.1992, active) |
| David Peterson | 474986 | David Peterson, **2B, b.1983, inactive** | **656849** (P, b.1995, active) |
| Luis Severino | 660876 | — | 622663 |
| Mike Burrows | 436639 | — | 681347 |
| Daniel Espino | 477425 | — | 682982 |

6 of 133 names (4.5%) resolved to a namesake. Identities confirmed by direct
`GET /api/v1/people/<id>` lookups; Sleeper had all six right.

## Root cause

`indexPerson` (`internal/playername/resolve.go`) writes the name key
unconditionally:

```go
rp.ByName[fullNorm] = p.ID
```

There is **no conflict detection and no tiebreak**. When a search returns several
players sharing a normalized name, the last one written wins. Two things make
that worse than a coin flip:

- The batched search deliberately spans `sportIds=11,12,13,14,16,1` (AAA/AA/A+/A/
  winter/MLB) and MLB's people-search returns **historical** players too, so
  common Latin American names reliably collide with retired or minor-league
  namesakes.
- The search batches run **in parallel** (`g.SetLimit(8)`), appending to `ids`
  in completion order, so which duplicate lands last is **nondeterministic**
  between runs.

A solo search for the same name returns the right player (verified live for all
three above) — batching is what introduces the ambiguity.

## Why this is worse than the rosterbot-i52 zeros

A failed resolution leaves `needsBackfill` set and shows up in the `failed`
count. A *misresolved* one does not fail: `fetchMLBGameLog` succeeds against the
wrong player, `computeFPtsFromGameLog` finds no entry for the date (the namesake
is retired), and the row is written as `FPts=0, HadGame=false` with
**`needsBackfill` cleared** — permanently recorded as a genuine off day. It is
invisible to every counter and every log line.

Where the namesake is *active* rather than retired, the failure mode is worse
still: a real stat line from the wrong human is scored as your player's day.

## Blast radius is not just the backfill

Five call sites share this resolver, and a wrong MLBAM ID is a wrong join key in
all of them:

- `internal/fantrax/mlb_backfill.go:29` — daily FPts backfill (feeds recap totals,
  `seasonToDateTeamMean`, the WP model, and the hitter blend window)
- `internal/recap/leaders.go:65` — League Leaders wOBA/FIP joins
- `internal/claims/enrich.go:46` — Statcast BUY-LOW/HOT tagging on pickups
- `internal/prospects/run.go:158,576` — prospect game logs

So a namesake collision can put another player's Statcast profile behind a waiver
recommendation, or another player's wOBA on the leaderboard.

## Candidate fixes

1. **Disambiguate on write.** When `rp.ByName[k]` is already set, prefer the
   active player, then the one whose sport is MLB, then the more recent debut.
   Never overwrite an active player with an inactive one. Cheap, local, and fixes
   every case measured here.
2. **Detect and report collisions** rather than silently picking. A name with two
   plausible claimants is exactly the case a human should see once.
3. **Prefer Sleeper's table where it carries `swish_id`** (the MLBAM id) — it is
   unambiguous by construction, one record per player. See `rosterbot-txw`; it
   was right on all six of these.

Fix 1 should land regardless of the Sleeper decision, since the search path
remains the fallback for prospects Sleeper has no MLBAM id for.
acceptance_criteria: indexPerson no longer silently overwrites a name key: on collision it prefers the active/MLB player deterministically, and the resolution is stable across runs despite parallel batching. Regression test pins the three verified cases (Jose Altuve->514888, Jose Ramirez->608070, David Peterson->656849) against a fixture containing both namesakes in both orders, so a last-write-wins reintroduction fails regardless of goroutine completion order.
close_reason: claimName now resolves namesake collisions toward the active player (lower-ID tie-break for determinism under parallel batching), and 'active' was added to the People.List WithFields mask — without it every p.Active is nil and the rule silently collapses to lower-ID-wins, so the fix would have been a live no-op. Verified live 2026-08-12 against Sleeper's independent MLB table over 133 real Fantrax names: ID disagreements went 6 -> 0, with all six (Jose Altuve, Jose Ramirez, David Peterson, Luis Severino, Mike Burrows, Daniel Espino) now matching Sleeper's verified-correct IDs. Regression test drives both arrival orders so a last-write-wins reintroduction fails regardless of goroutine completion order. Known residual: two ACTIVE namesakes remain genuinely ambiguous from a name alone; the tie-break guarantees a stable answer, not a correct one.

title: [bug] opsalert infra (OpsNotify Lambda + TaskFailRule) sat merged-but-undeployed through the entire 08-01..08-03 STALE_CLIENT outage
description:
During the rosterbot-7rl STALE_CLIENT outage (2026-08-01T13:01Z -> 2026-08-03T17:01Z, ~54 FAILED task runs across every Fantrax-touching job), NOT ONE Pushover alert fired. This was not a Streak/Overdue logic bug -- the alerting infrastructure that implements internal/opsalert simply wasn't deployed yet:

- Commit 889e67d ('feat(infra): EventBridge ECS task failure rule -> OpsNotify') merged 2026-08-01T02:05 UTC -- ~11 hours BEFORE the outage began.
- But InfraStack's last cdk deploy before the outage was 2026-07-31T21:43 UTC, and the next deploy wasn't until 2026-08-03T16:04 UTC -- a 2-day-18-hour merge-to-deploy gap that spans the ENTIRE incident.
- CloudFormation confirms: OpsNotify Lambda and TaskFailRule (the ECS-STOPPED EventBridge rule) both show CREATE_COMPLETE at 2026-08-03T17:07-17:08 UTC -- first-ever creation, ~90 minutes AFTER the outage had already ended (fix landed 17:01 UTC same day, pure coincidence of timing).
- HeartbeatRule (the Overdue 'job never launched' safety net) was created even later: 2026-08-04T00:37 UTC, the day after the outage ended.
- Confirmed via CloudWatch: zero AWS/Lambda Invocations for OpsNotify and zero AWS/Events TriggeredRules for TaskFailRule from 07-31 through 08-03T16:xx. The notifications/ feed shows exactly one entry in the whole 08-01/08-02 window (an 11:01 prospects report sent BEFORE the outage started at 13:01) -- silence after that. The only alerting Lambda live during the outage was the old build-only BuildNotify, which doesn't watch ECS task state at all.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE INCIDENT: this was luck of deploy cadence, not a one-off. Any infra-alerting feature that sits merged-but-undeployed is invisible exactly when the thing it's meant to catch happens to occur in that window -- and nothing today flags 'alerting infra is stale relative to main' the way make check-pins flags a stale nested go.mod. The 7rl outage happened to self-resolve same-day because someone was actively debugging it by hand; a quieter multi-day outage in this same undeployed window would have paged nobody.
design: Two independent angles worth considering, not mutually exclusive: (1) CD -- auto-deploy infra on merge to main (or at minimum a fast-follow deploy step in the same PR pipeline) so alerting-relevant infra changes don't sit merged-but-inert; (2) a drift check analogous to make check-pins/version-check that compares the deployed CFN stack's template hash (or a specific marker resource) against what's on main and fails loudly if they've diverged beyond some threshold. (1) fixes the root cause; (2) catches it if (1) is skipped for some future change.
acceptance_criteria: Either: a merge that touches infra/ triggers a deploy within some bounded window automatically, or a scheduled check flags when the deployed stack is N+ commits/days behind main on infra-relevant paths.

title: Recover draft-pick identity from the raw Fantrax trade payload
description:
MEASURED: unidentified picks gate 44% of trade verdicts (7 of 16 executed groups in this league). This is the single highest-leverage improvement to the Trades tab.

A pick row arrives as {fromTeam, toTeam, playerName:'', playerPosition:''}. Two fields are read into the go-fantrax structs and then DISCARDED by parseTransactionRow:
  - row.Result.Content (CellContent, never read)
  - any Cells entry whose key is not team/from/to/bid/priority/date/week

Dump the untouched GetLeagueHomeInfoRaw and TRADE-view payloads and check whether either names the pick. If one carries '2027 1st Round Pick', map it to HKB's 18 PICK assets (2027/2028, rounds 1-3, Early/Mid/Late, values 45-1419) and verdict coverage goes 56% -> ~100%.

Needs an authenticated fetch (chromedp).
notes: Re-measured 2026-08-10 against the refreshed trades cache (25 groups, was 16): 9 of 25 executed trade groups are pick-blocked = 36% of verdicts gated (previously reported 44% on the smaller corpus). Still the single highest-leverage follow-up — 0 name-misses, so picks are the ONLY thing suppressing a verdict. Reproduced independently in Python; matches internal/tradevalue/corpus_test.go exactly.
close_reason:
Fixed. The ticket's own hypothesis (Result.Content or a stray Cells entry) was wrong -- dumped the live TRADE-view payload and found pick identity in a separate row field, draftPickDisplayParts ({year, roundInfo}, both inline-HTML display strings), entirely discarded by the upstream parser.

Extended the go-fantrax fork (nixon-commits/go-fantrax@41eba54, pushed to bump-fantrax-api-185) to parse it into Transaction.{IsDraftPick, DraftPickYear, DraftPickRound, DraftPickNumber, DraftPickOriginalTeam}. Fantrax renders roundInfo two ways: "Round N (Team)" while the pick is still tied to a team's future standing, or "Round N Pick M" once the draft order is resolved -- the parenthetical team is the pick's ORIGINAL owner, not this trade's from/to (a pick can be re-traded before it's drafted).

rosterbot side: internal/hkb/picks.go adds PickAverage (means whichever of HKB's Early/Mid/Late tiers exist for a year+round) and Ordinal. internal/tradevalue.NewDraftPickAsset builds a priced, Estimated-flagged Asset from the recovered identity -- HKB prices picks by projected slot, not team, and there's no team-standing signal to pick one of the three tiers, so the average is used and flagged rather than presented as exact, same spirit as PackageDecay. internal/transactions wires this into the executed-trades path (newDraftPickTradePlayer); the pending-offers path (internal/tradeboard) is untouched since no live pending trade existed to confirm GetLeagueHomeInfoRaw encodes pick identity the same way -- left as a documented gap, not guessed at.

Measured impact, reproduced independently in Python against the same 25-group corpus: 15/1/9 (favors/too-close/incomplete) -> 18/3/4. 5 of the 9 pick-blocked groups carried a still-upcoming (2027) pick that's now priced (3 resolve to favors, 2 to too-close); the other 4 carried an already-resolved pick HKB no longer lists as upcoming, so they're named but stay unpriced by construction -- not a bug, a real data limit (that draft already happened; HKB doesn't retroactively price it). Coverage went from 64% to 84%, not literally ~100% as hoped -- the remaining 4 are unrecoverable without a point-in-time HKB snapshot from before that draft, out of scope here.

Also fixed the shared go-fantrax replace pin in lambda/go.mod (make check-pins was red after the root bump) and re-verified via make build-modules / make build. Full test suite green, corpus_test.go baseline updated with the new measured numbers and re-derivation rationale.

title: Dashboard headline metric (MAE) is near-blind to the model's actual skill
description: Measured over the 850 production grade rows (LEGACY + depthcharts-ros): hitter projections achieve MAE 4.380 vs 4.356 for a constant projection at the sample mean — i.e. -0.5% skill, and -6.0% against the MAE-minimising median baseline (4.132). Cause is that hitter projections barely vary (sd(proj)=0.66) against enormous daily outcome variance (sd(actual)=5.52). MAE at the player-day level is therefore ~all irreducible single-game noise, and the dashboard reports it to three decimals as the scoreboard. The model DOES have real skill, but only rank skill, which is exactly what a lineup optimiser needs: within-day Spearman rho = +0.1218 for hitters (se 0.0373, t=+3.26, positive on 30/40 days) and +0.4292 for pitchers (se 0.0982, t=+4.37, positive on 18/23 days). Both independently reproduced.
design: internal/report aggregates per (window,role); within-day rank correlation needs grouping by dt before correlating, which the current Aggregate does not do. The hindsight gap is the only metric denominated in points the league actually awards.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard leads with decision-relevant metrics: mean within-day Spearman by role, and the realized-vs-hindsight-optimal lineup gap that internal/backtest already computes. MAE remains available as a calibration diagnostic, not the headline.
close_reason: Shipped on feat/rosterbot-aei-rank-skill-headline (14 commits, 9b3a558..c206afc). Dashboard leads with a Decision quality block: points left on bench + lineup efficiency from the new durable Lineup Gap Store (internal/lineupgap, produced by grade, published as gap.json), plus within-day Spearman rho per role (tie-corrected average-rank, never pooled across roles, shown with +/-se and days-positive). MAE demoted to a Calibration diagnostics section carrying Metrics.SkillVsMean against a constant-at-sample-mean baseline. System comparison now ranks by rho descending with a combined-SE too-close-to-call gate. REPRODUCTION GATE PASSED on shipped code vs live Analysis Store (850 prod rows): hitters rho=+0.1218 se=0.0373 40d 30-positive; pitchers rho=+0.4292 se=0.0982 23d 18-positive -- all 8 statistics match the triage measurement, corroborated by an independent hand-written Python reimplementation. Three plan defects caught in review: flagBest crowned a leader when the runner-up's rho was merely uncomputable (bypassing the SE gate); ft.GetHitterSlots() did not exist (real method GetActiveSlots); minDayRows=5 was an unmeasured guess that discarded 15 of 23 usable pitcher-days -- calibrated to 3 by threshold sweep. make run-all 19/19 green; grade producer verified end-to-end locally (efficiency 79.4% over 3 days). NOT VERIFIED: dashboard never rendered in a browser -- repo has no JS test harness, so projections.js (+197 lines) is checked by syntax + hand-matched JSON contracts only.

title: recap-site runtime growing superlinearly — 30d TTL expires immutable past-period snapshots
description: recap-site wall time has grown 192s -> 266s -> 469s -> 483s -> 849s -> 1411s (2026-07-27), with per-week cost tripling from ~33s/wk to ~108s/wk. Mechanism verified from S3 cache object LastModified: 820 'cache/fantrax-pitcher-gs-*' and 817 'cache/fantrax-roster-stats-*' objects were rewritten on Monday 2026-07-20 alone, and the rewrite dates cluster exclusively on Mondays (2026-06-29, 07-06, 07-13, 07-20, 07-27) which is the recap-site schedule. Root cause: pastPeriodTTL = 30*24h at internal/fantrax/cached.go:23 applies to per-period snapshots that CLAUDE.md itself documents as immutable once the period closes. Every Monday rebuild therefore re-fetches every week older than 30 days from Fantrax, including the 200ms/day throttle at internal/fantrax/pitcher_starts.go:107. Cost is O(season length) and compounds weekly; the season runs to ~week 23.
design: Past-period snapshots are immutable by definition, so the natural fix is an effectively-infinite TTL for tierPast rather than 30d. Guard: DailyPeriodFor must be correct about which periods are actually past, otherwise an infinite TTL freezes a live period. Alternative: keep the TTL but make recap-site skip already-rendered weeks (dist/week-NN.html) unless forced.
acceptance_criteria: recap-site wall time stops growing with season length. Past-period snapshot cache entries are not re-fetched once written.
notes: Related but distinct: rosterbot-i52 covers the MLB statsapi game-log backfill failing at ~80% during the same bulk recap-site rebuilds. Different cache and upstream (mlbBackfillGameLogTTL=1h in mlb_backfill.go, vs this issue's pastPeriodTTL=30d in cached.go), so fixing tierPast's TTL here will NOT remove it — the 1h game-log TTL re-fetches every log on every run regardless. Same trigger, different mechanism. Both are the same CLASS of mistake though: a short TTL applied to immutable past data, so whoever fixes one should look at the other.
close_reason: PastPeriodTTL now unbounded + season-scoped keys + volatility guard on GetTeamPitcherStarts/tierForPeriod. Verified: settled-week recap 57.8s cold -> 2.8s warm, byte-identical output, warm state no longer expires. Six caller-side 30d literals collapsed onto fantrax.PastPeriodTTL (the ticket's cached.go:23 pointer covered only a quarter of the affected caches).

title: No alerting on scheduled task failure — 11-hour outage passed silently
description: The 2026-07-01T17:00Z to 2026-07-02T03:00Z incident ran 11 consecutive failed hourly 'optimize --matchup' runs plus the 23:41Z shadow (all exit=1, STALE_CLIENT) with no notification of any kind. Verified: 'aws cloudwatch describe-alarms' returns zero alarms and 'aws sns list-topics' returns zero topics in us-west-1. The buildnotify Lambda only fires on CodeBuild state-change events, so it covers image builds and not ECS task failures. optimize is the lineup-apply hot path — a silent multi-hour outage there means lineups silently stop being applied on game days.
design: Options: (a) EventBridge rule on ECS Task State Change with stoppedReason/exit code filter -> existing buildnotify-style Lambda -> Pushover; (b) CloudWatch alarm on a run-ledger-derived custom metric. (a) reuses the existing notify path and needs no new metric plumbing. Consider alerting on consecutive-failure count rather than each failure to avoid noise from a single transient.
acceptance_criteria: A repeated-failure signal reaches the operator's Pushover channel within ~2 consecutive failures of any scheduled task. Covers ECS task non-zero exit, not just CodeBuild.
close_reason: Shipped + deployed 2026-08-03. Merged 7d54b29; CodeBuild post_build cdk deploy applied it. Verified live: OpsNotify Lambda (60s) present, BuildNotify Lambda gone, TaskFailRule ENABLED on ECS Task State Change, and BOTH TaskFailRule and BuildNotifyRule target OpsNotify (detail-type dispatch). Stack UPDATE_COMPLETE 17:06:59.

title: League-wide projection grading: grade all 10 rosters, blended vs base, sliced by role/position
description:
## Problem

Projection-system grading is scoped to one team. `cmd/grade.go` calls `ft.DailyFantasyPoints(cfg.TeamID, ...)`, so each system is graded on ~35 player-days/day. Two consequences:

1. **Per-dimension slices are unusable.** `report.PositionRow` buckets C/INF/OF/UT/SP/RP, but our roster carries ~2 catchers — ~60 catcher-days a month. No claim about catcher (or any bucket) projection accuracy is supportable today. The per-role and per-bucket comparison is the actual goal of this work.
2. **We grade the blend, not the system.** `internal/lineuprun/snapshot.go:54` writes `sp.ExpectedPts` — the post-`BlendSources` value (FanGraphs base + trailing-30d/YTD Fantrax production). All four systems converge toward each other as the shared recent-production term takes weight (up to ~28% for hitters). We cannot currently measure whether blending helps or hurts.

Note the headline ranking is NOT the binding constraint: all four systems project the same player-days, so the comparison is paired and day-to-day FPts noise already cancels. Sample size buys the slices, not the top-line number.

## Goal

Grade every projection system against every rostered player in the league, on both the blended and the raw-base value, sliced by hitter/pitcher and by position bucket (C/INF/OF/UT/SP/RP), with a paired significance readout so slice differences are actionable. Enables (a) per-dimension system evaluation and (b) evidence-driven improvement of the blending model.
design:
## Decisions (settled in design interview)

**1. Grade both values per row.** `Projected` stays the blended value (unchanged meaning). Add `ProjectedBase` = raw system per-game projection. `MAE(blend) - MAE(base)` per slice is a first-class output — it is the only way to tell whether blending adds or destroys accuracy, and it directly serves 'improve the blending'.

**2. Population = the 10 fantasy rosters. Free agents are an explicit non-goal.** Rostered-player actuals are already-cached Fantrax bytes; FA actuals would require computing FPts from ~700 MLB statsapi game logs/day via the `mlb_backfill.go` path, which is built for a handful of fetches per window. Selection bias toward rostered players is consistent across all four systems so it does not corrupt the ranking — it only scopes the claim to 'accuracy on rostered players'. Accepted gap: waiver decisions concern unrostered players and get no grading signal (file separately).

**3. Reconstruct at grade time from `.archive/` — do NOT capture forward.** Decisive reason: reconstruction makes grading history **re-runnable**. A capture-based approach freezes every row at that night's blend formula, so a changed window or stabilization constant could only be evaluated going forward. Reconstruction is a pure function of archived bytes, so history re-grades in minutes under a changed hypothesis — the same property that let `backtest --recency-experiment` settle w30-vs-YTD (rosterbot-2nd), extended league-wide. Secondary: backfills to the archive start (~2026-07-02) instead of accumulating from ship date; adds no schedule, no task, nothing to the 23:40 shadow hot path.

Reconstruction needs no schedule/probables replay: `ExpectedPts` is a clean per-game value — `NonStarterSPDiscount` and `hasGame` gating are applied downstream in slot assignment (`internal/optimizer/pitcher_lineup.go:240`), not baked in.

The archive blob for date D is captured at `cron(15 14 * * ? *)` = 10:15am ET, **before any of D's games** — a strictly better grading capture point than shadow's 7:40pm ET.

**4. Extract the blend to a shared pure function.** `(base projection, recent-production series) -> blended per-game`, called by both `internal/lineuprun/blend.go` and the reconstructor. This eliminates the dual-implementation drift risk that plan 3 would otherwise introduce. `hitterWindowBounds` and `collapseHitterWindow` are already pure and client-free, so the extraction is cheap.

**5. Schema is additive columns, no new partitions.** On `analysis.GradeRow`: `ProjectedBase`, `DiffBase`, `FantasyTeamID`, `FantasyTeamName` (denormalized like `teamvalue.Row` so the read path needs no Fantrax call). Repurpose `Source` from snapshot/reconstructed (which goes constant under plan 3) to input provenance: `archive` vs `live-snapshot`. Partition path stays `grades/dt=X/system=Y/` — a third partition dimension means CDK + partition-projection enum churn for a 10-cardinality filter. Old rows carry zero `ProjectedBase` and remain readable. Purely additive: never rewrite existing partitions.

Volume is a non-issue and must not drive the design toward aggregation-on-write: 10 teams x ~40 rostered x 4 systems ~= 1,600 rows/day at ~200B ~= 320KB/day, ~58MB/season in 720 objects. Keep rows atomic.

**6. Scope becomes an explicit dimension in `report.Model`.** Re-key the maps from `window|role` to `scope|window|role`. Without this, league-wide rows silently change the detail views' population and **every trend line gets a step discontinuity on ship day** — pre-ship points are MAE on ~35 selected-for-good players, post-ship are MAE on ~400 including the league tail, drawn as one series. Per-view defaults: system comparison -> league; position table + calibration -> league (this is where N was too thin); misses list -> myteam (a league-wide misses list is 'who had a weird MLB day', not model quality); headline scorecard -> both side by side (the myteam-vs-league MAE gap quantifies how much easier our roster is to project). SPA gets a My Team / League toggle. The `myteam` scope preserves the existing series unbroken.

Scopes have different start dates — myteam-blended runs back to grading start; league-raw backfills only to ~2026-07-02; league-blended only as far back as per-team period snapshots remain fetchable. Charts must render a series beginning mid-axis without implying a drop to zero.

**7. Roster membership comes from `DailyFantasyPoints` per team, NOT `GetFullPlayerPool`.** The pool returns *today's* rosters; using it would retroactively attribute a waiver pickup to their current team for weeks they were not there. `DailyFantasyPoints(teamID, ...)` is derived from per-period roster snapshots and is point-in-time honest, and returns the actuals in the same pass. Team list from `GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams()`. This is the fan-out `recap.Run` already proves at `internal/recap/recap.go:104`.

**8. Expand `grade` in place; do not add a sibling command.** A second command means a second schedule, Fargate task, run-ledger entry and Infra row, plus a new failure mode ('grade ran but grade-league did not'), and would double-fetch our own team. Mitigations, both required: write my-team rows **before** the league pass starts (not batched at the end), and run the league pass under a context timeout with soft-fail — soft-fail alone covers errors but not hangs. Precedent: `cmd/projection-site.go`'s `renderValueSite` soft-fails independently of the accuracy dashboard deploy.

**9. Ship a paired significance readout, not just bigger numbers.** Without it, 10x rows produce four MAE values that *look* more authoritative while supporting exactly the same conclusions as today. Because all systems project the same player-days, compute the paired difference in absolute error per player-day and emit a confidence interval per slice: 'system X beats Y by N pts/player-day on SP, CI [a,b]'. This is what makes the per-dimension output a decision rather than a leaderboard.

## Non-goals (file separately)

- **Free agents / full player pool.** Leaves waiver-wire projections ungraded.
- **Ensemble / multi-system blending.** The store will hold everything an ensemble needs; evaluating an average or inverse-MAE weighting as a fifth pseudo-system is a follow-up. Do not couple a speculative modeling change to infrastructure that must land first.
- **Per-dimension system selection in production** (e.g. atc-ros for SP, steamer-ros for OF). Requires `BlendSources` to hold multiple simultaneous sources. Depends on this bead — do not commit to acting on a per-slice signal before seeing whether the differences are significant.
- **Blend parameter tuning** (30d window, 250-PA constant, 30%/35% floors, SP 15GP / RP 25GP). The re-gradeable history this bead creates is the prerequisite.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Blend logic exists as one pure function consumed by both `internal/lineuprun` and the grade-time reconstructor; no second implementation of the blend.
- [ ] `grade` writes rows for all 10 fantasy rosters, carrying `FantasyTeamID`, `ProjectedBase` and `DiffBase`; existing partitions are not rewritten.
- [ ] Roster membership per date is point-in-time correct (a mid-window waiver pickup is attributed to the team that held them on that date, not today's holder) — covered by a test.
- [ ] Reconstruction validated against the live snapshot for our own team: per-day drift metric emitted, with a documented tolerance justified by the 10:15am-vs-7:40pm archive/shadow capture gap.
- [ ] My-team rows are committed before the league pass runs; league pass is under a context timeout and soft-fails without losing my-team rows — covered by a test.
- [ ] `report.Model` keyed by `scope|window|role`; the `myteam` scope reproduces today's dashboard numbers exactly (no step change in any existing trend line on ship day).
- [ ] Dashboard exposes a My Team / League toggle with the agreed per-view defaults, and renders a series that starts mid-axis without a false drop to zero.
- [ ] Per-dimension paired comparison shipped: for each (system pair, slice) a paired mean absolute-error difference with a confidence interval. Slices: hitter/pitcher and C/INF/OF/UT/SP/RP.
- [ ] Every position bucket reaches a usable monthly N league-wide (C is the binding constraint at ~15/day vs ~2/day today).
- [ ] Backfill run via existing `grade --dates 2026-07-02:<today>`; no new backfill command. Daily `--window 3` continues to self-heal.
- [ ] `make run-all` passes; `go vet ./...` and `go mod tidy` clean.
notes:
Design settled via /grill-me interview 2026-07-26. Key premise correction recorded in the Problem section: sample size is not the binding constraint on the headline ranking (paired comparison already cancels daily FPts noise) — it is the binding constraint on the per-position slices, which is what this work is actually for. If the top-line ranking barely moves after shipping, that is the expected result, not a failure.

Related: rosterbot-2nd (windowed-recency strategy replay) established the re-gradeable-history pattern this extends. ADR-0002 (team value store accumulates forward) is the contrasting case — that store has no backfill because rosters are not archived; this one does, because `.archive/` holds the FanGraphs inputs and `DailyFantasyPoints` reconstructs historical rosters.

title: Split Fantrax period numbering into WeeklyPeriod/DailyPeriod types
description: Fantrax exposes two unrelated numbering schemes — a weekly matchup axis (ScoringPeriod.Number, ~7 days/period) and a daily roster/apply axis (DailyPeriodFor, one per calendar day) — both represented as a bare int. Nothing at a call site distinguishes them, so a weekly value passed where a daily one is required type-checks silently. This exact bug class caused two production incidents (rosterbot-uv6, rosterbot-z3b) and a third instance is currently open (rosterbot-ren: internal/fantrax/daily_fpts.go uses the naive PeriodForDate instead of the anchored DailyPeriodFor for historical dates).
design: Introduce type WeeklyPeriod int and type DailyPeriod int in internal/fantrax. Update every period-carrying signature to declare its axis: FindCurrentPeriod/FindJustEndedPeriod/GetGSLimits/ScoringPeriod.Number -> WeeklyPeriod; DailyPeriodFor/ApplyLineup/GetHitterRosterForPeriod/GetCurrentPeriod -> DailyPeriod. Thread the types through downstream call sites in internal/lineuprun, internal/gscheck, internal/recap, cmd/backtest.go, cmd/grade.go (~40-50 call sites total, ~20 signatures in internal/fantrax). Go's lack of implicit conversion between named int types means every mismatch becomes a compile error.
acceptance_criteria: All period-carrying function signatures in internal/fantrax use WeeklyPeriod or DailyPeriod instead of bare int. go build and go vet pass. daily_fpts.go's naive PeriodForDate usage is migrated to the anchored DailyPeriodFor or explicitly documented as the accepted rosterbot-ren gap.
close_reason: WeeklyPeriod/DailyPeriod type split landed; historical FP/GS walks now resolve dates via the authoritative periodList map (dailyPeriodForDate). Class-A unification deferred to rosterbot-2ax.

title: GS-check false whole-league Under-Min alert: GetTeamGS used weekly period numbering for daily snapshot diff
description:
## Symptom
On 2026-07-13 the daily gs-check Pushover alert reported '10 violation(s) · max 12, min 10' with ALL 10 teams 'Under Min' at 0–5 GS — for a completed normal week (period 15, 07-06..07-12). No real team starts only 0–5 pitchers in a week whose min is 10.

## Root cause
GetTeamGS reconstructs per-day GS by diffing consecutive DAILY YTD roster snapshots; getPlayerGSSnapshotForPeriod is keyed by the daily scoring period (one number per calendar day, e.g. 104..110 across a week). Commit 92ed478 (rosterbot-uv6) routed the day-walk through fantrax.ResolvePeriod, whose tier-1 (FindCurrentPeriod over the weekly SCHEDULE periods) returns the WEEKLY matchup number (15) for every day in the week. So every day fetched the same daily snapshot #15 (mid-April!), all day-over-day deltas collapsed to 0, and each team's weekly GS under-counted to ~one day's worth (0–5). The limits (min 10/max 12) were correct; the tallies were broken.

Verified live: fixed GetTeamGS yields realistic period-15 tallies (8–13 GS; only 2 teams genuinely under min), vs the broken 0–5.

## Fix (this issue)
Reverted GetTeamGS's walk + baseline to DAILY numbering via gsPeriodWalk/dailyPeriodFor (AnchorPeriodForDate anchored on GetCurrentPeriod, else PeriodForDate) — the same daily numbering its working sibling GetTeamPitcherStarts uses. Dropped the unused periods param from GetTeamGS (+2 callers). Rewrote gs_period_walk_test.go to assert daily numbering. The uv6 test asserting [16]x14 encoded the bug and was removed.

## Follow-up (separate)
The uv6 concern was that a merged multi-day WEEKLY period (All-Star break, period 16 = 07-13..07-26) needs care. The daily numbering handles it correctly IF Fantrax's DAILY periods advance one-per-day through the break. That is unvalidated for the future ASB dates. Validate empirically near 2026-07-27 (when period 16 is first gs-checked) that daily periods 111..124 map to 07-13..07-26 without merges; if Fantrax merges daily periods across the break, GetTeamGS/GetTeamPitcherStarts may need the actual daily-period date map. Filed as [[rosterbot-asb-daily-validate]] context.
acceptance_criteria: gs-check reports realistic per-team GS for a completed normal week (tallies near/above the weekly min, not ~0); only teams genuinely below min are flagged. Unit test locks in daily-numbering walk. Live-verified for period 15.
close_reason: Merged in PR #49 (commit 67e4387) — GetTeamGS reverted to daily-period numbering, live-verified for period 15.

title: GetTeamGS mis-derives period number for every day inside a merged multi-day scoring period
description:
internal/fantrax/gs_check.go's GetTeamGS builds a periodFor closure (lines ~176-184) that resolves each day in its walk via AnchorPeriodForDate(today, currentPeriod, d) -- plain day-by-day anchor arithmetic assuming exactly one scoring period per calendar day. But the ScoringPeriod (sp) GetTeamGS is called with can itself be a merged multi-day period: TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod (internal/fantrax/gs_check_test.go) already fixtures this exact case -- period 16 spans 2026-07-13 to 2026-07-26 (14 calendar days under one period number) for the All-Star break. That merged period starts TOMORROW relative to when this issue was filed (2026-07-12).

GetTeamGS backs both internal/gscheck.RunGSCheck (league-wide GS violation detection, gs-check command) and cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget gate (weekly game-start limit awareness, optimize command when GS_TRACKING_ENABLED=true) -- both live production paths. There is no existing test coverage for GetTeamGS's walk across a merged period.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use the periods fixture from TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod: period 16 spans StartDate=2026-07-13, EndDate=2026-07-26; period 17 starts 2026-07-27.
2. Call GetTeamGS with sp=period 16 (the merged period), today=2026-07-27 (the day after it ends), and a GetCurrentPeriod() result of 17 (so periodFor uses AnchorPeriodForDate(2026-07-27, 17, d) for each day d in the walk).
3. Observe periodFor(2026-07-13) = 17 + (13-27) = 3, periodFor(2026-07-14) = 4, periodFor(2026-07-20) = 10, periodFor(2026-07-25) = 15 -- all wrong; only periodFor(2026-07-26) = 16 (the day nearest the anchor) happens to be correct.
4. Each wrong period number is a real period elsewhere in the season (e.g. period 3 is an actual April date), so getPlayerGSSnapshotForPeriod(teamID, period) silently returns a real but unrelated day's roster/GS snapshot instead of erroring -- the corruption is silent, not a crash.
design: Thread the already-fetched periods []ScoringPeriod list into GetTeamGS (both callers -- gscheck.go and cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block -- already have it in scope after rosterbot-z3b) and replace the periodFor closure's AnchorPeriodForDate/PeriodForDate pair with fantrax.ResolvePeriod(periods, currentPeriod, seasonStart, today, d) -- the same periods-list-first resolver rosterbot-z3b introduced for the apply path. This requires changing GetTeamGS's signature to accept periods (or a resolver function) as a parameter.
acceptance_criteria: A test using the existing TestFindCurrentPeriod_MergedAllStarBreakPeriod-style fixture (period 16 spanning multiple calendar days) verifies GetTeamGS's day-by-day walk resolves every day in the merged span to the correct period number, not just the day nearest the anchor. Both GetTeamGS callers (gscheck.RunGSCheck, cmd/optimize.go's GS-budget block) pass their already-fetched periods list through. Existing GetTeamGS tests continue to pass.
notes: Discovered by code-reviewer subagent during rosterbot-z3b's review (2026-07-12), not part of that issue's original scope -- filed separately per reviewer recommendation given the time-sensitivity (this season's period 16 merge starts 2026-07-13, the day after filing).
close_reason: gsPeriodWalk resolves the merged-period walk via ResolvePeriod; code-reviewed, tested, shipped ahead of period 16 opening 2026-07-13.

title: Stop .beads jsonl merge conflicts on every PR (union merge driver)

Real sync is Dolt over sync.remote git refs; jsonl is export-only (no-db:false). Fix: commit .gitattributes with 'merge=union' on both files -> git stops raising conflicts, post-merge hook re-exports clean from Dolt. Verified via git check-attr (merge: union).
