title: Validate whether hitter/pitcher YTD blend beats a bounded window or no-blend baseline
description:
Two independent audit agents (fantasy-baseball-model-auditor and fantasy-baseball-strategist, 2026-07-10) independently flagged the same risk: internal/projections/blended.go and pitcher_blended.go blend the base FanGraphs RoS projection (depthcharts-ros, which already incorporates 2026 YTD performance with proper regression) with RAW, unregressed season-to-date FP/G. At ~90 GP for a regular, seasonWeight=approxPA/(approxPA+250) is already ~58%. This risks double-counting the same in-season signal and over-reacting to hot/cold streaks.

I extended cmd/backtest.go's --recency-experiment harness (previously ytd/w14/w30/decay21 only) with a 'base' variant (no blend at all, pure depthcharts-ros) to isolate the effect, and ran it live:

  --matchup (last completed week, 2026-06-29..2026-07-05, 7 days):
    base    realized=387.0  meanGap=-19.14
    ytd     realized=405.0  meanGap=-16.57  (current production strategy — WON this week)
    w14     realized=340.0  meanGap=-25.86
    w30     realized=396.0  meanGap=-17.86
    decay21 realized=389.0  meanGap=-18.86

  --weeks 4 (2026-06-15..2026-07-09, 25 days):
    base    realized=1252.0 meanGap=-23.76
    ytd     realized=1226.0 meanGap=-24.80  (current production strategy — worse than base AND w30)
    w14     realized=1151.0 meanGap=-27.80  (clearly worst)
    w30     realized=1261.0 meanGap=-23.40  (best of all 5 variants)
    decay21 realized=1217.0 meanGap=-25.16

Over the longer window, current production (ytd/season-to-date) is beaten by both a bounded 30-day window AND a no-blend baseline. The single-week result flips the other way, consistent with a real-but-modest, sample-dependent effect rather than a huge bug. 25 hitter-days is still a small sample for a strategy decision that affects every lineup every day.
acceptance_criteria: Run --recency-experiment over a much longer window (full season to date, or --weeks 8+) to get a stable read. If w30 (or base) continues to beat ytd, either (a) switch BlendedSource's recent-stats input from unbounded season-to-date to a bounded rolling window, or (b) blend against a preseason (independent) projection instead of an in-season-updated RoS system, or (c) lower the recent-weight ceiling. Extend the same experiment to pitchers (pitcher_blended.go) — the current harness is hitters-only. Update CLAUDE.md's Blended scoring section once a decision is made.
notes: Tooling change (the 'base' variant + HasProjDiag n/a-vs-0.00 fix in internal/backtest/strategy_replay.go and cmd/backtest.go) already committed. This issue is about acting on what the tool shows, not about the tool itself.
close_reason: Shipped: internal/lineuprun/recent.go windowedHitterRecent + projections.WindowWeight(30) live; w30-beats-YTD decision + pitchers-stay-YTD recorded in CLAUDE.md Blended scoring section.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Determine whether the production hitter/pitcher recent-performance blend is actually improving lineup decisions versus simpler alternatives, and act on the finding.

**Current behavior:**
The blend combines the season-long base projection with the player's raw season-to-date performance, weighted increasingly toward recent performance as the season progresses. A strategy-comparison tool exists that can replay several alternative strategies (no blend at all, various rolling windows) against actual historical lineup outcomes. A short initial comparison run showed the current strategy losing to both a no-blend baseline and a bounded 30-day window over a 4-week sample, but winning over a single-week sample — not enough data to be confident either way.

**Desired behavior:**
A confident, data-backed answer on whether the current blend strategy is the best of the available options for both hitters and pitchers, backed by a much larger sample than what's been checked so far, followed by either confirming the current approach or switching to whichever alternative the data supports.

**Key interfaces:**
- The existing strategy-comparison tool already supports adding/removing named strategies to compare; extending it to pitchers (currently hitters-only) is straightforward if needed.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The comparison has been run over a much larger sample (full season to date at minimum) for hitters.
- [ ] A decision has been made and recorded: keep the current strategy, or switch to a specific alternative, with the reasoning captured.
- [ ] If a change is made, it's verified not to regress recent lineup outcomes before being treated as the new default.

**Why this needs a human, not an agent:**
This changes a formula that determines every lineup's point projections, every day, for the rest of the season — a live, standing decision with real competitive stakes, not a self-contained bug fix. "How much data is enough to be confident" and "which alternative to prefer if several look close" are judgment calls the maintainer should make directly rather than delegate. An agent CAN be asked to do the mechanical part (re-run the comparison tool over a longer window and report the numbers back) as a preliminary, lower-stakes step if useful — that sub-task would itself be ready-for-agent even though the decision that follows isn't.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the blend formula's underlying shrinkage math (the plate-appearance-based weighting curve itself) — that's a separate, deeper design question from "which recency window to blend."

title: Remove GS_MAX/GS_MIN static env vars; source everything live from Fantrax
description: Now that GS budget/gscheck fetch real limits live from Fantrax (rosterbot-r10), the GS_MAX/GS_MIN numeric env vars only ever served as a fallback value + feature toggle. Replace with a single GS_TRACKING_ENABLED boolean toggle; on live-fetch failure, send a Pushover alert (PUSHOVER_USER_KEY) instead of falling back to a stale static number. Also remove GS_MAX/GS_MIN from infra/infra.go's ECS secrets and the AWS SSM parameters. Discovered along the way: internal/lineupapi (used by the Lambda in lambda/) transitively imports internal/fantrax, and lambda/go.mod had no replace pin for the go-fantrax fork branch, so cdk synth was already broken on main since PR #29 merged — fixed as part of this work.

title: Measure cold bd build time in a cloud session; restructure setup script if it does not cache
description:
docs/cloud-sessions.md ships a setup script that installs bd (beads) by
building it from source:

  go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@v1.0.4

bd links Dolt and produces a ~200MB binary, so this is the long pole of the
script. The Claude Code cloud environment requires the setup script to finish
in roughly five minutes for the environment cache to build; if it overruns,
the environment silently stops caching and EVERY session pays the full build
again.

This was never measured. The session that wrote the script never got a clean
cold-build timing, and the current layout (build backgrounded, `go mod
download` run alongside, then `wait`) is a guess at staying under the budget
rather than a measured fit.

WHAT TO DO
1. Create a fresh cloud environment and time the setup script cold — no warm
   module cache, no warm build cache. Record the wall time of the
   `go install` specifically, not just the script total.
2. Confirm whether the environment cache actually built (a second session
   starting fast is the observable signal).
3. If it does not cache, move the bd install OUT of the setup script. Options,
   roughly in order of preference:
   - fetch a prebuilt bd release binary instead of building from source, if
     one exists for the platform;
   - move the install into the SessionStart hook, which already detects a
     missing bd and prints the recipe — it would pay the cost once per
     session but not block environment caching;
   - drop bd from cloud sessions entirely and rely on the hook's existing
     "file follow-ups in your reply" fallback.

CONTEXT
The pin is v1.0.4 (matches the operator's laptop). @latest is v1.2.1, which
is newer than this repo's refs/dolt/data and offers to migrate a database
shared with every clone — so bumping the pin to dodge a build-time problem is
NOT a safe fix on its own.

Filed from the branch that rebased and verified claude/lineup-age-hkb-heatmaps
onto main; bd was unavailable in the cloud session that wrote the doc, so
nothing could be filed at the time.

title: P5: pilot ops - admin Tenants tab, failure taxonomy, signup disclosure
description:
What makes a pilot with other people's teams operable.

ADMIN TENANTS TAB: per tenant - last run, streak verdict, conn_status, last successful apply, auto_apply state. This is how 'what is failing' gets answered across N tenants without reading the ledger by hand.

FAILURE TAXONOMY, routing by who can act:
  tenant-actionable  expired token, needs_reconnect, login_challenge, team gone
                     -> that user's in-app feed
  operator-actionable bug, AWS failure, STALE_CLIENT
                     -> Jon's Pushover
Without this you become the help desk for expired tokens users could fix themselves.

SIGNUP DISCLOSURE - this is a shipping artifact, not a nicety. Two things were decided that users must be told plainly before enrolling:
  - we store their Fantrax password (decision 4)
  - the admin can read any tenant's data, including trade valuations (decision 13)
Jon is a competitor in this league. A leaguemate who would decline that deserves to decline it before handing over credentials, not after.

title: P1: session carries subject and version; revocation via token_version
description:
session.go's sessionPayload carries ONLY {exp} today - there is no notion of whose session it is. Add sub (uid) and ver (int), verified against USER#<uid>.token_version.

Revoking every device for a user = increment token_version. SessionSecret rotation stays the nuclear option that logs out everyone.

The Dynamo read this implies is NOT additional cost on tenant-scoped routes - they must load the user record anyway to scope their query. It is genuinely additional only on passthrough routes (/v1/trades), where it is one GetItem against a table with a dozen items. Do not cache it; that is premature and adds an invalidation problem.

Existing sessions (no sub) must be rejected, not silently treated as the operator.
close_reason: Shipped and verified in production: ghost-user and stale-TokenVersion sessions both 401.

title: User settings page: connect Fantrax, set Sleeper league, per-user preferences
description:
The per-user surface where a tenant configures their own accounts, replacing the deployment-level env vars that configure the single operator today.

BLOCKED BY PHASE 1 (identity substrate). There is no user record to hang settings on until USER#<uid> exists in DynamoDB. Do not start this before that lands.

## What is per-user vs what stays a deployment constant

The pilot scope (design decision 19: one team per user, one league) already fixes several of these, and the page must not become a dump of every env var. Current deployment-level config:

  FANTRAX_USERNAME/PASSWORD  -> PER USER. This is the connect form (decision 3).
  FANTRAX_TEAM_ID            -> PER USER, but NOT typed by the user. It comes from
                                the invite (minted against a team) and is PROVEN at
                                connect time via TeamRosterResponse.MyTeamIDs. The
                                settings page displays it; it is not an input.
  FANTRAX_LEAGUE_ID          -> STAYS a deployment constant. One league at pilot scope.
  FANTRAX_IL_SLOTS           -> STAYS. League config, same for every tenant.
  FANTRAX_MINORS_SLOTS       -> STAYS. Same.
  SLEEPER_LEAGUE_ID          -> OPEN QUESTION, see below.
  DYNASTY_FORMAT             -> PER USER preference (sf_dynasty default). The Dynasty
                                Value Store already carries all four formats on every
                                row, so this is purely a display choice - cheap to make
                                per-user.
  FOOTBALL_PUSHOVER_*        -> deferred; v1 is in-app feed only (decision 14).

## The Fantrax and Sleeper halves are asymmetric, and the page should say so

Fantrax needs credential custody: the user types username+password, the API Lambda encrypts under KMS (it holds kms:Encrypt only), an ECS connect task decrypts and drives chromedp to mint FX_RM. Sleeper needs NOTHING - its public API takes no key, so 'connecting' Sleeper is just pasting a league id. Presenting them as two equivalent 'connect your account' cards would misrepresent what the user is handing over. The Fantrax card is the one that needs the disclosure text (decision 13: admin can read tenant data; and that we store their password).

## OPEN QUESTION to resolve before building

Is Sleeper also one-league-per-deployment, or per-user? Baseball was scoped to one league because the whole optimizer assumes this league's scoring/slots. Football is READ-ONLY (no lineup writes exist on the Sleeper side), so a per-user Sleeper league is far cheaper than a per-user Fantrax league - there is no optimizer to reconfigure, only a value store and a trade monitor. That asymmetry may make per-user Sleeper worth doing even while Fantrax stays single-league. Decide explicitly rather than inheriting baseball's constraint by default.

## Contents

- Fantrax: connect form; conn_status (pending/verified/needs_reconnect) with the
  reason; reconnect button; the bound team_id shown read-only.
- Sleeper: league id (pending the question above); dynasty format selector.
- Preferences: auto_apply toggle - OFF by default and the one control that changes
  whether the bot writes to their roster (decision 11). It needs real weight in the
  UI, not a checkbox in a row of them.
- Account: display name, email (admin-attested, read-only), link to the existing
  Passkeys tab rather than duplicating it.

## Build notes

Follow web/dashboard/views.js and football.js: createElement/textContent, never
innerHTML. value.js predates that rule and uses innerHTML + an escapeHtml that does
not escape quotes, so it is unsafe in attribute context - do not copy it.

The settings write path is the first authenticated POST in the dashboard that mutates
per-user state. It needs the rate limiting noted in the design (per-user cap on the
connect endpoint specifically, because repeated failed Fantrax logins trigger account
lockout - the same reason decision 17 forbids blind retry).
acceptance_criteria:
- A logged-in tenant can connect Fantrax from the page and see conn_status transition pending -> verified without leaving it (polling GET /v1/runs/{id}/progress, which already exists).
- A failed connect shows the failure CLASS (bad credentials / login_challenge_or_timeout / team mismatch), not a generic error.
- team_id is displayed, never typed, and a connect whose MyTeamIDs does not contain the invited team is rejected.
- auto_apply defaults OFF for a new tenant and the UI states plainly what turning it on means.
- The Sleeper-vs-Fantrax asymmetry is visible: connecting Sleeper never asks for a credential.
- Settings POSTs are rate limited per user; the connect endpoint has its own tighter cap.
- No innerHTML in the new JS.

title: Stale-branch content check is defeated by drift adjacent to the branch's change
description:
Follow-up to rosterbot-rx4, reproduced in production within an hour of rx4 merging.

rx4 replaced file-name attribution with a reverse-apply of the branch's own patch against main. That answers 'does main already carry this change' only while the surrounding context still matches.

Merging the crq epic (PR #140) put crq.3's reports/ grants at infra/infra.go:269, immediately above feat/trades-tab's two GrantRead lines at 279-280. The lines themselves were still on main -- the branch was landed -- but the patch stopped reverse-applying, so the check returned indeterminate, and rx4's deliberate fail-closed policy alerted anyway. Same false positive, new route: 'STALE: feat/trades-tab - 91h stale - infra/infra.go'.

FIX: when the reverse-apply is inconclusive, fall back to the weaker but position-independent question -- is every line the branch ADDED present in main's copy of the file? Only when some are missing is it genuinely indeterminate.

GUARD: require at least one 'substantive' added line (not blank, not pure punctuation) before concluding landed. A lone brace is present in main for reasons unrelated to the branch, and concluding 'landed' by coincidence is this alert's one unacceptable failure -- silence.

Validated against the real case: reverse-apply fails, fallback finds substantive=2 missing=0 -> LANDED, alert suppressed. Two new tests (drift case + trivial-only guard); 9 total green.

title: CodeBuild: concurrent builds race the CFN stack, and the failure is misattributed to the next step
description:
Two pushes to main close together produce two concurrent CodeBuild runs against one CloudFormation stack. The second one's 'cdk deploy' is refused:

    Stack:arn:aws:cloudformation:us-west-1:476646938644:stack/InfraStack/... is in UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS state and can not be updated.

Observed live 2026-08-13: build 5760e089 (commit 70ae7ff, 14:00:14) and build 20400a18 (commit 09d6ca9 / PR #139, 14:01:01). The first succeeded end to end; the second failed.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS.

1. The race itself. Nothing serializes builds. CodeBuild has a concurrent-build limit setting (ConcurrentBuildLimit: 1) that would queue the second instead of failing it.

2. The failure is reported against the WRONG STEP, which is the more expensive problem. buildspec.yml's cdk block is:

       - |
         cd infra && cdk deploy -c enableBuild=true --require-approval never --outputs-file ../cdk-outputs.json
         cd ..

   There is no 'set -e' in that block, so a failed cdk deploy does not fail the command. Execution proceeds to the NEXT block, which begins 'set -eu' and immediately dies on the missing file:

       FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'cdk-outputs.json'

   CodeBuild therefore names the dashboard-sync block as the failing command, and the phase-context message quotes that block in full. The actual failure was cdk deploy, ~90 seconds earlier, in a different step. Diagnosing this required reading the raw CloudWatch stream and filtering for the stack error; the build's own failure message actively misleads.

Impact of this instance was nil - PR #139 touched only .github/scripts/, its image still reached ECR (docker push precedes cdk deploy), and the earlier build had already synced the dashboard and run projection-site. But main's HEAD showed a red build and a Pushover fired for a deploy that did not need to happen.
acceptance_criteria:
- A failed 'cdk deploy' fails the build at that step, with cdk's own error as the reported failure (add 'set -e' or '&&' chaining to that block).
- Concurrent builds do not fail on the stack lock: set ConcurrentBuildLimit=1 on the CodeBuild project so a second push queues behind the first.
- Verify by pushing twice in quick succession and confirming the second build queues and then succeeds, rather than failing.
notes:
2026-08-14: second instance, different mechanism. Build for 7a3108e failed at PROVISIONING (no logs, no code executed) three minutes after the build for 3c271dc succeeded, and a third build for a1dfdff started three minutes after that. Not the CFN stack lock this bead was filed for -- CodeBuild could not start the container at all -- but the same root cause: several builds queued close together with no concurrency limit. ConcurrentBuildLimit=1 would serialize both failure modes.

Impact was nil because the next build carried the same commits, but the failure is indistinguishable from a real one at a glance: main's HEAD showed red and a Pushover fired for a build that had executed nothing.

title: Stale critical-path branch check re-flags landed branches once main touches the same file
description:
The stale-branch alert (rosterbot-v4l mitigation) fired every 6h for four days on a branch whose content had already landed.

SYMPTOM: 'feat/trades-tab - 87h stale - infra/infra.go' pushed via Pushover on every scheduled run since 2026-08-12T18:52Z. The branch's entire infra/infra.go contribution is two lines (GrantRead trades/*, tradevalues/*), both present on origin/main at infra/infra.go:279-280. Nothing was unlanded.

ROOT CAUSE: check-stale-critical-branches.sh intersects still_differs with branch_changed at FILE granularity, but the property it needs is content-level. The squash-merge guard clears a landed branch only while main leaves the file alone; the direction guard excludes only files the branch never touched. When BOTH sides touch one file, it survives both filters permanently.

PROOF (branch held constant, only base moved):
  base=312a90f~1 -> still_differs empty -> PASS
  base=origin/main -> still_differs=infra/infra.go -> ALERT
Timeline matches: check PASSED 08-12T15:52Z, then 312a90f (16:30Z) and a80968e (16:50Z) touched infra/infra.go for unrelated dynasty-football work; every run since 18:52Z failed. Reported age is the branch's own last-touch, which never moves, so it never ages out.

SEVERITY: alert fatigue on the channel that exists because nothing paged through the 54-run 08-01..08-03 outage.

FIX: per-file content attribution via reverse-apply of the branch's own patch against main's copy; three-state (unlanded/landed/indeterminate) with indeterminate reported rather than dropped, matching the never-degrade-to-silence posture of rosterbot-00e and rosterbot-chs. Two new tests: the landed case (reproduces the false positive) and a false-negative guard proving unlanded work in a shared file is still flagged.

NOTE: this check answers branch-vs-main (unlanded), not deployed-vs-main (undeployed) which rosterbot-v4l's acceptance criteria actually asked for. That gap remains open under v4l.

title: Overdue cannot discover a tenant whose job never launched
description:
Residual gap of the rosterbot-ys8 class, surfaced while implementing rosterbot-crq.1.

opsalert.Overdue now keys by (command, user_id) and correctly reports a tenant that ran and then went dark. But it discovers the tenant set FROM THE LEDGER - it cannot report a tenant that has never produced a single record, because Schedule carries a cadence, not a roster, and internal/opsalert is a stdlib-only leaf that cannot enumerate users.

So: a manager is onboarded, their EventBridge fan-out is misconfigured, their job never launches even once -> no ledger record -> no tenant discovered -> perfect silence. Which is exactly the failure Overdue exists to prevent, one level down.

This is a known, documented limit (see the Overdue doc comment), not an oversight in crq.1. It cannot be closed without the tenant roster, which does not exist until Phase 1 (identity substrate).

Fix direction: feed the active tenant roster to the notifier the same way the cadence table already reaches it - infra/infra.go builds JOB_SCHEDULES from the crons it declares precisely so a tolerance restated in Go cannot drift from its schedule. The roster wants the same treatment, but sourced at runtime (it changes on signup, unlike the crons). Options: an env var refreshed by the fan-out Lambda, or the notifier reading the identity store directly - the latter costs opsalert its stdlib-only leaf property, so prefer the former.

Do this in Phase 4 (fan-out), alongside the cron-enumerates-tenants work.
acceptance_criteria:
- A tenant with zero ledger records for a scheduled per-tenant job is reported as Missed.
- opsalert remains a stdlib-only leaf (verify with go list).
- The roster reaches the notifier by the same mechanism as the cadence table, so it cannot drift silently from the actual tenant set.

title: Identity writes lose a passkey under concurrency (no compare-and-set)
description:
Registration and login both read-modify-write the whole Identity record with a blind overwrite.

  handleAuthRegisterFinish: GetIdentity -> append credential -> PutIdentity   (webauthn.go:139-153)
  handleAuthLoginFinish:    GetIdentity -> update sign counter -> PutIdentity (webauthn.go:199-204)

No optimistic concurrency anywhere. IdentityStore.PutIdentity is a straight overwrite (identity.go:80-89, FileIdentityStore; same shape in s3lineup).

At N=1 with one device this is benign. With multiple devices - or any N>1 - a concurrent login and registration silently LOSES a passkey: both read the same record, both write, last writer wins and drops the other's change. The user sees a successful registration that later isn't there, with no error anywhere.

Worth fixing before the multiuser epic rather than during it: it is a real bug today, and the fix shapes the DynamoDB item design (conditional write on a version attribute).
acceptance_criteria:
- Identity/user records carry a version attribute; writes are conditional on it and retry on conflict.
- Test: concurrent register + login against the same identity -> both changes survive, or the loser retries and succeeds. No silent drop.
- Applies to whichever store backs identity after Phase 1; if fixed before Phase 1, FileIdentityStore and s3lineup both honor it.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed on claude/multiuser-passkey-auth-8ee4c9. Not yet merged to main, not deployed.

title: Use statsapi season player dumps as a bulk name→MLBAM index, search as fallback
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Replace the MLB people-**search** with a season-scoped **bulk player index** as the
primary name → MLBAM-ID path, keeping the existing search only as a fallback.

## The primary key is not the problem

MLBAM ID already IS the primary key, and we already resolve to it — Savant, the
game logs and `internal/statcast` all key on it. What is weak is the *name → key*
step, which today is a fuzzy, batched, rate-limit-exposed **search** across
`sportIds=11,12,13,14,16,1` that returns historical players and therefore
collides on common names. `rosterbot-bms` fixed that with a heuristic
(active beats inactive). A bulk index removes the ambiguity **structurally**
instead.

## Measured 2026-08-12, over the same 133 real Fantrax names

| source | resolved | ambiguous | missed | payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| statsapi **search** (current, post-bms/i52) | 132 | 0 *by heuristic* | 1 | ~6 batched calls/resolution, 186 resolutions per recap-site build |
| statsapi **season dumps** (union of sportIds 1,11,12,13,14) | 128 | **0** *structurally* | 5 | **8.2 MB**, 5 requests, ~0.3 s each |
| **Chadwick Bureau register** | 132 | **18** | 1 | 65 MB, 16 shards |

`GET /api/v1/sports/{1,11,12,13,14}/players?season=2026` returns 5,722 unique
players (1,378 MLB + 7,255 minor-league rows before dedup) with every name
variant statsapi knows: `fullName`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `useName`,
`useLastName`, `boxscoreName`, `nameSlug`, `fullFMLName`, `middleName`.

**The season scope is the whole point.** Verified directly: the retired
`Jose Altuve` (501447) and inactive `Jose Ramirez` (691342) are **absent** from
every 2026 dump, while the active 514888 / 608070 are present. The namesake
class that produced `rosterbot-bms` cannot occur against this index — zero of
133 names mapped to more than one player. That replaces a heuristic with a
guarantee.

Prospect coverage is fine: Sam Antonacci (803011) is present.

## The catch, measured rather than assumed

The dumps are **not** a complete list of active players. Jordan Westburg (676059)
and Reese Olson (681857) both report `active: true` from `/people/<id>` yet
appear in **none** of the five dumps. That is why the bulk index scores 128 and
not 133.

So this is a **primary + fallback**, not a replacement: look up in the bulk index
first, fall through to the existing (now namesake-corrected) search for misses.
That composition resolves 132/133 — same as today — with zero namesake ambiguity
and roughly two orders of magnitude fewer upstream requests on a bulk
`recap-site` build.

## Why NOT Chadwick as the resolver

The Chadwick Bureau register is the real purpose-built crosswalk (129,658 rows
carrying `key_mlbam`) and it *is* a proper ID database — but it is **historical**,
which makes it actively worse for this job: **18 of 133** names were ambiguous,
three times the collision rate of the search we just fixed, and it would need the
same active-player filter layered on top. It also costs 65 MB against 8.2 MB.

Its real value is a **different** join we currently do by name:

- `key_fangraphs` — present on **21,184** rows. `internal/projections` matches
  FanGraphs to Fantrax by normalized name today; this is a true crosswalk.
- `key_bbref` (23,781) and `key_bbref_minors` — no current consumer.

That is worth its own ticket, not this one.

## The residual neither source fixes

`"Jake Latz"` is a **Fantrax-ism**. Statsapi has `fullName: "Jacob Latz"`,
`useName: "Jacob"`, `nickName: null` (656641); Chadwick has `name_first: Jacob`,
`name_given: "Jacob Eugene"`, `name_nick` **empty**. No identity database closes
this, because it is not an identity gap — it is a colloquial spelling only
Fantrax uses. Options are a small local alias table or a last-name +
first-initial fallback accepted only on a unique match. Track separately.

## Acceptance

Bulk index built from the five season dumps, cached (they change slowly — daily
TTL), consulted before the search; search retained for misses. Reproduce the
table above over the full league player pool, not just this 133-name sample, and
show: resolved / ambiguous / missed for index-only, search-only, and combined.
The combined figure must be >= today's 132/133 with ambiguity 0, or the change
is not worth making.

title: Explore Sleeper MLB player dump as primary name→MLBAM-ID source (parity check vs statsapi search)
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Explore replacing the MLB statsapi **name-search** resolver (`internal/playername.ResolveMLBAMIDs`)
with a **bulk player table** from Sleeper's MLB player dump as the primary
Fantrax-name → MLBAM-ID source.

## Why this is worth exploring

`ResolveMLBAMIDs` answers "what is this player's MLBAM ID?" by *searching* an
upstream API, batched 25 names at a time, keyed in cache by a hash of the input
name set. That architecture is the root of `rosterbot-i52`, and the diagnosis
there (2026-08-11) found three defects that are all downstream of it:

1. A transient search failure yields a **partial result cached as authoritative
   for 7 days** — `fetchAndResolve` never returns an error, so `cache.Get` stores
   it. Three cached entries with **zero** resolved players exist in production,
   all written during one 2026-07-31 bulk-build hour.
2. The search is sent the **raw** name while dedup/matching use the normalized
   one. Measured live: `"A.J. Blubaugh"` → 0 results, `"aj blubaugh"` → 1.
   `"Zach Cole Jr."` → 0, `"zach cole"` → 2. Inverted for hyphens:
   `"Ha-Seong Kim"` → 1 raw, 0 normalized. Neither form is a superset.
3. The cache key is the input **name set**, so reuse is near zero — one
   `recap-site` build produced **186** separate resolutions.

There is also a latent hazard specific to search: go-mlb's `WithNames` joins the
batch into a single comma-delimited `names` query param
(`go-mlb@v0.1.2/options.go:363`). Any raw name containing a comma — the
`"Guerrero, Jr."` form `playername.Normalize` explicitly handles — splits the
batch and corrupts that request's results.

A bulk table makes all of that structurally impossible: one fetch either succeeds
or fails, matching happens locally against a complete name table using our own
`Normalize`, and there is no per-name-set cache key to explode.

## Existing groundwork

`internal/sleeper` **already exists** — added on branch `feat/dynasty-football`
(commit `97f9e4d`, closed `rosterbot-2i7`) as a zero-dep read-only leaf, and it
already implements exactly this pattern:

- `baseURL = "https://api.sleeper.app/v1"`, a `var` for test override
- `PlayersNFL()` — the full `/v1/players/nfl` dump (~14.6 MB) through
  `cache.FileCache[T]` at 24h, with the explicit "never fetch it in a loop" note
- hermetic table-driven tests against recorded fixtures

So an MLB sibling is a **small extension of a proven leaf**, not a new client.

## What to verify (this is the exploration)

- Does `/v1/players/mlb` exist, and what is its size and shape? Confirm before
  assuming symmetry with the NFL endpoint.
- Does each record carry an **MLBAM cross-reference** (`mlb_id` or similar)? The
  whole proposal rests on this; without it Sleeper gives names but not the ID
  `fetchMLBGameLog` needs.
- **Minor-league and prospect coverage** — this is the crux. The current resolver
  searches `sportIds=11,12,13,14,16,1` (AAA/AA/A+/A/winter/MLB) precisely because
  the rows needing resolution skew toward callups, prospects and waiver adds. A
  table covering only 40-man MLB rosters would resolve the easy names and miss
  exactly the hard ones.
- **Update latency** for a fresh callup or signing. `backfillDailyFPts` runs on
  players who *just* appeared, so a table refreshed weekly would be worse than a
  live search for the newest names.
- Does it bridge the nickname gap? The one residual miss that normalization
  cannot fix is `"Jake Latz"` → MLB's `"Jacob Latz"`. If Sleeper carries both a
  common and a legal name, that class resolves for free.

## Likely outcome shapes

- **Primary, with statsapi search as fallback** — bulk table for the 95%+ it
  covers, live search only for names it misses. Keeps prospect coverage while
  removing nearly all request volume. This is the expected best answer.
- **Cross-check only** — load both, log disagreements, decide later. Cheapest way
  to measure coverage before committing.
- **Reject** — if MLBAM cross-references or minor-league coverage are absent,
  Sleeper cannot be primary and the ticket closes with that measurement recorded.

## Risks

- Third-party dependency with no SLA, for data currently sourced from MLB itself.
- Sleeper's MLB product is far less prominent than its NFL one; coverage and
  freshness should be **measured, not assumed**.
- Requires `feat/dynasty-football` merged to main (or `internal/sleeper`
  cherry-picked) before this can build on it.

## Relationship to rosterbot-i52

Not a substitute. `i52`'s fix (retry + refuse-to-cache-degraded + raw/normalized
search fallback + split failure counters) should land regardless — the
poisoned-partial-cache defect is a property of *any* resolver that soft-fails,
and this ticket may well conclude that a fallback search path is still needed.
This is the strategic follow-up that could remove most of the request volume that
makes those failures likely in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: A measured parity report exists comparing Sleeper's MLB player table against our current resolver over a real Fantrax name set (full league player pool + the backfill's flagged names, which skew to callups/prospects). Report must state, as counts not impressions: (1) how many names Sleeper resolves that statsapi search does, (2) how many it resolves that search misses, (3) how many search resolves that Sleeper misses — broken out for MLB vs minor-league/prospect names, since prospect coverage is the deciding factor. Ticket closes with an explicit verdict: primary-with-search-fallback, cross-check-only, or reject — justified by those numbers.

title: [bug] Hitter blend recency window is team-scoped — newly acquired players get a truncated GP and a ~100% base weight
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

The hitter blend's recency window is built from **our own team's** per-period roster
snapshots, so a player's "games in the trailing 30 days" is really "games *while on
our roster* in the trailing 30 days". For a just-acquired player those are wildly
different numbers, and nothing downstream distinguishes them.

## Mechanism

`windowedHitterRecent` (`internal/lineuprun/recent.go`) calls
`ft.DailyFantasyPoints(teamID, start, end, ...)` — a walk over **one team's**
`fantrax-roster-stats-<teamID>-<season>-<period>` snapshots. `WindowedRecent`
(`internal/projections/recency.go`) then groups the result by player:

```go
for _, d := range days {
    for _, p := range d.Players { series[p.PlayerID] = append(...) }
}
```

A player absent from a day's snapshot contributes **no `DayFP` row at all**. There is
no "did not play" vs. "was not ours yet" distinction, so pre-acquisition days are not
zero-weighted — they are invisible. `RecentStat` carries only `{FPtsPerGame, GamesPlayed}`
(`internal/fantrax/recent_stats.go:13`), so window coverage is never recorded and cannot
be checked by any consumer.

`GamesPlayed` then drives the blend weight (`hitterBlendWeights`,
`internal/projections/blended.go:74`):

```
approxPA     = GP * 3.8
seasonWeight = approxPA / (approxPA + 250)
baseWt       = max(1 - seasonWeight, 0.30)
```

Truncated GP -> `baseWt` pinned near 1.0. `BlendMinGP` defaults to 2, so 2 days of
tenure is enough to clear the guard and blend a 2-game sample.

## Reproduction (confirmed, exact numeric match)

Observed on the 2026-08-11 hitter pipeline board. Team `a2u7l4hwmj203yvz`.
Counting cached `fantrax-roster-stats` periods per player (139 periods available,
window = periods 136-139 since `hitterWindowBounds` ends at yesterday):

| Player | Periods on our roster | Displayed Mix | GP implied by Mix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sam Antonacci | **136-139 (4)** | 96% | 3 |
| Zach Neto | **136-139 (4)** | 94% | 4 |
| Nico Hoerner | 1-139 (139) | 73% | ~24 |
| Randy Arozarena | 1-139 (139) | 74% | ~23 |

Antonacci also appears in team `8msu09qbmj203yvz`'s snapshots continuously from period
10 — the production exists, it is just filed under the team that owned him.

Solving the weight formula backwards reproduces the board exactly:
GP=3 -> `1 - 11.4/261.4` = **0.956 = 96%** (Antonacci);
GP=4 -> `1 - 15.2/265.2` = **0.943 = 94%** (Neto).
Both match the displayed cells to the rendered precision, which confirms roster tenure
(not playing time) is what produced them.

## Why this matters

**1. The number is ambiguous, and that is what was noticed.** Carson Williams shows 96%
after **70** periods of tenure — a genuine low-sample prospect, and the correct reading.
Antonacci shows the same 96% after **4** periods. Identical cell, opposite meanings: one
is "we have data and he barely plays", the other is "we have almost no data". The
operator cannot tell them apart, and neither can any consumer of `RecentStat`.

**2. The measured edge is forfeited exactly when it is most consequential.** Zach Neto is
an everyday MLB shortstop; with full window coverage he would sit near Hoerner's ~24 GP
and ~73% base. He reads 94%, so the recency signal `rosterbot-2nd` measured as worth
~1 realized pt/game/day is effectively switched off — for the players a trade just made
the hardest to value.

**3. The residual blend is noise, not signal.** Antonacci's `-0.18` adjustment is drawn
from a 3-game sample applied at 4% weight. Small in magnitude, but it is not the quantity
the blend is documented to compute.

This self-heals after ~30 days of tenure, so it is transient — but it recurs on every
acquisition, and it is silent: no warning, no log line, no failure. Same class as
`rosterbot-8dl` (a metric structurally pinned near one value, correct code, blind result).

## Candidate directions (not a decision — for triage)

- **(a) Widen the source to league-wide.** Fetch every team's snapshots for the window so
  coverage follows the *player*, not our roster. Snapshots are already per-(team, period)
  cached at `PastPeriodTTL`, and `recap`/`recap-site` already pay this cost for all teams,
  so warm-cache cost may be near zero. Cold cost is ~12 teams x 35 periods on the hourly
  path. Overlaps with `rosterbot-tr1`, which needs the same league-wide walk.
- **(b) Extend the existing MLB-statsapi backfill.** `backfillDailyFPts` already
  reconstructs a day's FPts from a game log x league weights for first-appearance rows;
  extending it to fill the pre-acquisition days of the window is bounded to newly
  acquired players only. Risk: `rosterbot-i52` reports that path failing at ~80% during
  bulk rebuilds, so it would be leaning on known-flaky machinery.
- **(c) Floor: make the truncation visible.** Carry window-coverage days on `RecentStat`
  alongside `GamesPlayed`, and mark the Mix cell when coverage < window
  (`formatBlendMix`, `internal/lineuprun/display.go:120`, already has a dim-grey
  convention for the no-recent-data case). Does not fix the weight, but stops 96%-from-
  no-data reading identically to 96%-from-low-playing-time.

(c) is strictly smaller than (a)/(b) and is not mutually exclusive with either — it could
ship first as disclosure, mirroring how `rosterbot-8dl` was mitigated.

## Files

- `internal/lineuprun/recent.go` — `windowedHitterRecent`, team-scoped fetch
- `internal/projections/recency.go` — `WindowedRecent`, absent day == no row
- `internal/projections/blended.go:74` — `hitterBlendWeights`
- `internal/fantrax/recent_stats.go:13` — `RecentStat`, no coverage field
- `internal/lineuprun/display.go:120` — `formatBlendMix`

Pitchers are unaffected in this specific form: `GetRecentPitcherStats` reads a single
roster snapshot whose `FantasyPointsPerGame` is cumulative **YTD from Fantrax**, which
covers the player's whole season regardless of tenure. Worth confirming rather than
assuming — a newly acquired pitcher's YTD GP may still be Fantrax-team-credited.
acceptance_criteria: A player acquired mid-window either (1) has their recency window populated from league-wide data / statsapi backfill so GamesPlayed reflects actual games played in the trailing 30d, or (2) is visibly distinguishable in the pipeline board and in RecentStat from a rostered-all-window player with genuinely low playing time. A regression test pins the distinction: two players with identical GamesPlayed but different window coverage must not render identically.
close_reason: Fixed via remedy (b): coverImportedHitters detects mid-window acquisitions (first appearance after the 30-day window start) and rebuilds their recency entry from the new fantrax.MLBDailyFPts game-log read, replacing the roster-tenure-truncated one. Verified live 2026-08-12: Sam Antonacci 96%->74% and Zach Neto 94%->74% (everyday-player band, ~23 GP vs 3), while genuine low-sample players correctly stayed high — Carson Williams 94%, Angel Genao 92%, Spencer Horwitz 89%. Stable across back-to-back runs. Coverage is now reported unconditionally on stderr and names unmatched players; the one unmatched case (Marcelo Mayer) was verified legitimate — resolves to 691785 but has no MLB game since 2026-06-25, so nothing to backfill. MLBDailyFPts deliberately kept separate from DailyFantasyPoints: grade/backtest/recap must not be credited with production earned on another roster.

title: internal/dynasty: per-player value store, Aggregate, and model
description:
Store + model in ONE package, following internal/lineupgap's shape ('since the model is a few dozen lines') rather than the teamvalue/valuereport split.

Row grain is PER-PLAYER — one row per (date, team, asset), ~360 rows/day, ~20 MB/year. This is a deliberate departure from the baseball Team Value Store: per-player grain keeps every future breakdown re-derivable, so the artifact is NoBackfill:FALSE (a missed day is re-runnable), unlike docs/adr/0002.

Carry all four format values as leaves (sf_dynasty/non_sf_dynasty/sf_redraft/non_sf_redraft) so the renderer derives the toggle client-side — the pattern teamvalue.Row establishes.

Aggregate joins rosters -> bundle by Sleeper ID (EXACT — no name normalization), buckets by position and asset_type (player|pick), computes starters value from the league's own roster_positions, and records matched/rostered plus unmatched names as a json:"-" diagnostic per teamvalue.Row.Unmatched.

Picks: reconstruct owned picks from traded_picks + settings.draft_rounds, priced at StatsGuy's 'mid' variant, disclosed. Measured: 58 traded-pick records in the live league, zero outside StatsGuy's priced grid.

HEADLINE IS STARTERS VALUE. Full-roster total ships demoted (gate pre-commitment — see bd memory dynasty-football-coverage-gate-2026-08-10).

Reuses teamvalue.Aggregate's bucketing (positions.IsPitcherSlot for pitcher, pp.MinorsEligible for minors) rather than re-deriving it. Suppressed alongside the verdict when the offer is 'incomplete'.
