close_reason: Closed

title: Roster-shape pitcher denominator is structurally pinned near 100% — cannot see pitcher surplus
description:
The roster-shape block shipped in rosterbot-hx5 reports, per side, the share of deployable projected value the roster fielded. The hitter half works. The pitcher half currently conveys no roster-shape signal.

Measured by an independent Python reimplementation over the 68-snapshot corpus in .backtest/snapshots/ during the rosterbot-hx5 final review:

- The pitcher predicate (IsStarter || GSSuppressed for SPs, HasGame for RPs) admits ~25% of pitcher hasGame projected value, range 11-44%. The hitter predicate admits ~87%.
- On 2026-08-06 the pitcher denominator was 2 players / 12.40 pts against 13 rostered pitchers / 117.9 pts of hasGame value. Four SPs who were OCCUPYING ACTIVE P SLOTS (Burns 17.5, Perez 16.7, Cavalli 16.0, E-Rod 15.5) were excluded from BOTH terms, as were two benched SPs with games.
- Over the trailing 22 days the deployable pitcher count exceeded the 6 P slots on exactly ONE day. Absent a GS-gate firing, the pitcher side can only read 100%.

Consequence: a roster carrying 13 pitchers against 6 slots — a 2.2x surplus, precisely the imbalance the feature exists to surface — prints 'Pitchers fielded 100% of owned projected value (0.0 stranded)'. On its headline question the block says the opposite of the truth.

Mitigated but NOT fixed in rosterbot-hx5: the block now prints per-side coverage ('pitchers 2 of 13 rostered player-days deployable') plus a caveat sentence, so the rate cannot be misread as 'no surplus'. The denominator itself is unchanged.

Root cause is a framing choice, not a coding error. Pitcher surplus is a WEEKLY, GS-cap-bound phenomenon; the daily deployability frame is nearly always satisfiable because only ~2 SPs are probable per day against 6 slots. Note the naive weekly framing has the same blindness: if the gate never fires, weekly fielded == weekly owned == 100%. gs_suppressed is false on all 68 snapshots, though the field is only days old, so 'the gate never fires' is not yet established.
design:
Three candidate directions, none yet chosen:

1. Include rest-day SPs at optimizer.NonStarterSPDiscount (0.05x) rather than excluding them. In-repo precedent: backtest.pitcherOptimalPts (internal/backtest/backtest.go:294-308) solves the identical 'SP whose team played but who did not pitch' problem exactly this way, so this would also make internal/backtest treat one modelling question one way. Cost: at 0.05x the stranded figure is small (six rest-day SPs at ~0.9 each), so it measures 'rest-day SPs are nearly worthless' more than 'I own too many aces'.

2. Weekly frame keyed to the GS cap: starts the rotation could supply over the window vs starts the cap let you field. Directly pairs with the constraint that actually binds. Cost: the two sides then measure over different time frames, and it inherits the same blindness whenever the gate does not fire.

3. Measure slot occupancy rather than value deployment for pitchers: of the 6 P slots, how many held a pitcher who actually pitched. Sidesteps the projection-value question entirely.

Prerequisite for choosing: real gs_suppressed history. The field only exists from 2026-08-05, so re-measure once there is a month of it and check whether the gate fires in production at all (GS_TRACKING_ENABLED is false in local dev, which is why every local run shows no suppressions).
acceptance_criteria: The pitcher rate responds to pitcher roster surplus: a roster carrying materially more pitching than 6 P slots plus the weekly cap can deploy reads materially below 100%, and the choice of denominator is documented with the measurement that justifies it.

title: Nothing enforces the go-fantrax fork pin agrees across root and lambda go.mod
description:
rosterbot-7i3 collapsed the API VERSION to one site, but execution found the PIN moved up a level rather than disappearing: the fork pseudo-version now appears in go.mod:62 and lambda/go.mod:69 with nothing enforcing agreement. (opsnotify's was dead and was deleted in 8ce9de1.)

make build-modules caught the drift during rosterbot-7i3 ONLY because that bump added exported symbols. In the actual recovery scenario — bump auth_client.APIVersion's string, no API change — a stale lambda/go.mod compiles clean, CI is green, and the Lambda ships the old constant. version-check cannot detect it either: the probe validates the root binary's pin only.

Currently unreachable in practice: lambda pulls internal/fantrax for fantrax.Slot only, constructs no client, issues no /fxpa/req. So this is latent, not live — but it is a restatement of the exact defect class rosterbot-7i3 was filed against.
acceptance_criteria: A CI check fails when the replace directives for github.com/pmurley/go-fantrax disagree between root go.mod and lambda/go.mod.
close_reason: make check-pins added; wired into make build + ci.yml. Mutation-verified red/green.

title: InvalidatePeriodRosterCache builds the pre-season-scoping key and invalidates nothing
description:
rosterbot-qoa (commit 44a8029, 2026-07-31) moved every past-tier cache key to <prefix>-<teamID>-<season>-<period> via seasonScopedKey. internal/fantrax/client.go:297-298 was not updated: it still builds cache.Key(keyHitterRoster, c.teamID, periodStr) = fantrax-hitter-roster-<teamID>-<period>, the old grammar, while GetHitterRosterForPeriod writes through cachedForPeriod -> seasonScopedKey with the season segment.

So the two period-specific Invalidate calls have targeted a key that does not exist since 2026-07-31. Its stated purpose — 'Called after ApplyLineup so a second optimize run sees the updated lineup rather than the stale pre-apply snapshot' — is silently not happening.

Found while pruning the orphaned pre-rename objects for rosterbot-ngg: the keys this function deletes ARE those orphans, which is how the mismatch surfaced.

The two UNSCOPED calls on lines 300-301 (fantrax-{hitter,pitcher}-roster-<teamID>, no period) are still correct — those keys carry no season by design, and they were observed being removed in production on 2026-08-03.
design:
Fix is to route the period-specific keys through the same seasonScopedKey the writer uses. That needs the season, which cachedForPeriod resolves lazily via periodCachePolicy(period) — so the invalidation should resolve it the same way rather than assuming the current calendar year, or the fix reintroduces the same class of drift one layer up.

Better still: the mismatch was possible because the reader and the invalidator each build the key by hand. A single unexported keyer used by both would make this unrepresentable — the same argument seasonScopedKey itself is built on.
acceptance_criteria: After ApplyLineup, a second optimize run for the same date re-fetches the roster rather than reading the pre-apply snapshot, and the CLAUDE.md idempotency check (same inputs twice -> 'No changes needed') holds when the two runs are less than 15 minutes apart. A test pins the invalidated key against the key cachedForPeriod writes.
notes:
Blast radius is bounded by TTL, which is why it has not been loud. The period key sits at tierToday (15m) for the current and last three periods (periodIsVolatile), so a stale post-apply snapshot self-heals within 15 minutes and the hourly Lineup runs are 60 minutes apart. The exposure is a second optimize run inside that 15-minute window — which is exactly what CLAUDE.md's idempotency check prescribes ('run the command twice with the same inputs and confirm the second run shows No changes needed'), so that verification is currently unsound after an apply.

Possibly related to rosterbot-cem (hourly optimize 64% no-op, 75% of applied moves are re-flips), though cem predates the rename and cannot be caused by it.
close_reason:
Fixed by routing both sides through one key builder rather than correcting the key. periodCacheKey(prefix, teamID, period) now returns the key and its tier from a single periodCachePolicy read; cachedForPeriod and InvalidatePeriodRosterCache both call it, so the writer and the invalidator cannot drift again — which was the actual defect, not the wrong string.

Confirmed the bug behaviourally before fixing: the new test fails red against the old code with 2 fetches where 3 were expected, i.e. the invalidation dropped nothing. It drives the real reader (cachedForPeriod, what GetHitterRosterForPeriod calls) instead of comparing key strings, because a string comparison would have to be rewritten to match any future refactor and would keep passing while the behaviour broke. A second test pins the current-day keys, which carry no season by design (todayTTL, no period number) and had to keep the plain grammar — the fix must not sweep them into season scoping and break them the other way.

Verified: red-then-green, full suite green across all four modules, go vet clean, and two back-to-back live optimize --dry-run runs byte-identical ending in 'No changes needed'. Caveat recorded honestly: --dry-run never calls InvalidatePeriodRosterCache (it runs only after a real ApplyLineup), so that is a read-path regression check, not an end-to-end proof of the apply case. The unit test is what covers the apply case.

The acceptance criterion's second half — the CLAUDE.md idempotency check holding for two runs less than 15 minutes apart — follows from the unit test but was not exercised against production, since doing so would mean applying a real lineup twice.

title: grade --window 3 leaves permanent holes when an outage runs longer than 3 days
description: The STALE_CLIENT outage (2026-08-01..08-03) failed every Fantrax-touching job for 3 days. grade's default --window 3 re-grades trailing days ending yesterday, so the run on 08-04 covers 08-01..08-03 and self-heals those — but 2026-07-31 fell outside the window and would have stayed a permanent hole in BOTH the Analysis Store and the Lineup Gap Store. The Lineup Gap Store half was recovered by hand (grade --dates 2026-06-16:2026-08-02, run 2026-08-03); analysis/grades/ for dt=2026-07-31..08-02 is still missing because the local .backtest/snapshots-systems/ copy does not cover those dates — it needs a run with the S3 backtest/ prefix synced down.\n\nThe self-heal window is silently narrower than the outages it is meant to absorb, and opsalert escalates at 3 consecutive failures — i.e. exactly when the window has already been outrun. Options: widen the default window, derive it from the newest partition already present rather than a fixed count, or have the Infra tab's gap detection drive a targeted re-grade.
notes: RECOVERED 2026-08-03 22:20Z: dt=2026-07-31 grades restored by pulling only the four S3 backtest/snapshots-systems/system=*/2026-07-31.json files locally and running grade --dates 2026-07-31:2026-07-31. Wrote exactly 5 objects — 4 new grade partitions (22 rows each, all versions=1, nothing clobbered) plus an idempotent rewrite of the 07-31 gap row (-14.0, unchanged). Snapshot generated_at was 2026-07-31T23:42Z = 19:42 ET, so it cleared the sameETDate stale guard. Analysis Store now covers through dt=2026-07-31. dt=2026-08-01 and 08-02 remain permanently ungradeable (shadow never captured them). NOTE for anyone repeating this: do NOT sync the whole backtest/ prefix down and re-grade a wide range — the local .backtest/snapshots-systems/ copy on this machine stops at 2026-07-26 and is an OLDER capture than prod for overlapping dates, which is how a broad grade --dates run silently rewrote dt=2026-07-21 with one fewer row per system (restored from S3 object versioning, which is Enabled on the state bucket).

title: Fantrax API version has two pin sites and no detection — STALE_CLIENT has taken prod down twice
description:
The Fantrax client version is hardcoded in two places that must move together:
1. fork github.com/nixon-commits/go-fantrax auth_client/fantrax_client.go — const fantraxAPIVersion (unexported)
2. rosterbot internal/fantrax/gs_check.go — the one /fxpa/req payload we build ourselves rather than via the library's buildFullRequest

Nothing enforces that they agree. If only the fork moves, GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams alone starts returning STALE_CLIENT — which breaks gs-check, recap and team-values while optimize keeps working, a confusing partial outage.

This has now caused two full outages:
- 2026-07-01..07-02, 12 failed runs (180.0.0 -> 181.0.0, fork PR #6)
- 2026-08-01..08-03, 53+ failed runs (181.0.0 -> 185.1.0, rosterbot-7rl)

Each recovery needs a cross-repo dance: bump fork, push fork, bump rosterbot go.mod replace, bump gs_check.go, merge, deploy.

DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE of the rosterbot-7rl hotfix, which was kept to the minimum change that restored service.
design:
Two independent improvements, either or both:

A. COLLAPSE THE PIN SITES. Export the constant from the fork (auth_client.APIVersion) and have gs_check.go reference it instead of a literal. Additive and cheap — the fork is already ours. Removes one of the two things that must move together. A cheaper variant needing no fork change: route the standings call through auth_client's buildFullRequest like every other call, deleting our hand-built envelope entirely. Worth checking why it was hand-built — likely just needs a msgs shape the wrapper didn't expose.

B. DETECT RATHER THAN PIN. The current version is machine-readable from the web app's embedded package.json, which is how 185.1.0 was found: fetch https://www.fantrax.com/, extract main-<HASH>.js, extract its chunk-*.js list, grep for {name:"fantrax",version:"N.N.N"}. A startup probe that reads this and falls back to the pinned constant on any error would make the bump self-healing. Risks to weigh: it adds a network dependency to client init, the bundle layout can change (it is not a stable API), and a wrong auto-detected value would be harder to debug than a stale constant. Probably right as a WARNING path — log/alert when detected != pinned — rather than as the live value.

Note the detection gap is separately addressed: the opsnotify ECS task-failure alerting on branch fix/rosterbot-naz-task-failure-alerting would have paged on the 3rd consecutive failure instead of this going unnoticed for two days. It is unmerged. That is the highest-value follow-up here and is not blocked by this issue.
acceptance_criteria: The Fantrax API version appears exactly once in source, or a mismatch between pin sites fails a test/build rather than surfacing as a partial production outage.
close_reason:
Version pin collapsed to one site. gs_check.go's hand-built /fxpa/req envelope was byte-identical to the fork's unexported buildFullRequest — nothing needed a different shape, it was hand-rolled only because the helper was lowercase. Exported APIVersion/BuildFullRequest/ReadBody from the fork (5cbe633); gs_check.go now uses them and carries no version literal. grep -rn '185\.1\.0' --include='*.go' returns nothing.

It also bypassed the fork's readBody, which is why the August outage reported itself as 'no response data in standings' rather than STALE_CLIENT — half of what made that partial outage confusing was the wrong error message, not just the split pin. Fixed too.

Detection needed no bundle scrape: one unauthenticated POST discriminates cleanly (verified live both directions — 185.1.0 -> WARNING_NOT_LOGGED_IN, 181.0.0 -> STALE_CLIENT), because Fantrax checks the version gate ahead of auth. Asking whether OUR pin still passes has a yes/no answer and nothing to get wrong; the 151-chunk scrape stays a human recovery step in the runbook. New version-check command runs daily at 10:30 UTC and exits non-zero ONLY on STALE_CLIENT, riding the existing ledger -> opsalert -> Pushover path with no new notification code.

FOUND DURING EXECUTION: the issue said two pin sites; there were four. lambda/go.mod and opsnotify/go.mod each carried their own go-fantrax replace, stale at e5d491d — two commits behind, predating even the 181->185 bump. make build-modules was failing branch-wide until fixed. Verified compile-time only (opsnotify has zero fantrax in its dep graph, since deleted; lambda pulls internal/fantrax for fantrax.Slot alone, no client, no /fxpa/req) so no production version mismatch occurred. Nothing yet enforces those go.mod pins agree — filed as rosterbot-00e.

Follow-ups: rosterbot-00e (pin-agreement CI check), rosterbot-0a1 (version-check is fail-silent on VersionUnknown).

title: Hindsight-optimal can score BELOW actual — positive lineup gap is mathematically impossible
description:
backtest.RunLineupAnalysis produced Gap = +7.0 for 2026-07-02 (actual 48.0, optimal 41.0, started_n 12, benched_n 1), observed in the Lineup Gap Store after backfilling 2026-06-16..2026-07-27 (45 days, 1 occurrence).

A positive gap is impossible by construction. Gap = ActualPts - OptimalPts, and the lineup we actually ran IS a feasible slot assignment, so the hindsight optimizer should always be able to reproduce at least that total. optimal < actual means the optimizer could not reconstruct an assignment that Fantrax accepted.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE DAY. This is not a cosmetic sign error -- it means OptimalPts can be under-computed. Everywhere it is under-computed the gap is understated and lineup efficiency is OVERSTATED. Season efficiency currently reads 76.4% (3511/4596 over 45 days); the true figure is at most that and possibly lower. The same hindsight path feeds the recap's per-team efficiency and 'points left on bench' numbers, so any under-count skews those too.

LIKELY CAUSES, in rough order:
1. Position-eligibility drift -- a player was started in a slot the optimizer's EligibleForSlot rejects (INF/UT handling, or eligibility that changed after the fact), so hindsight cannot place them.
2. Slot-count mismatch -- ActualPts sums every player with p.Active && p.HadGame, while OptimalPts sums only players the optimizer seats. If the actual roster had more active+playing players than the optimizer has slots for, actual exceeds optimal trivially.
3. Pitcher path -- optimizePitchers feeds probableStartersFromActuals and may discount or exclude an SP that actually started.

2026-07-02 is a small day (13 graded rows, 12 started) which makes it tractable to diff by hand.
design:
First step is a diff, not a fix: for 2026-07-02, dump the actual seated lineup (player, slot, FPts, eligibility) alongside the optimizer's chosen assignment and find which player the optimizer failed to seat. That single row should identify which of the three causes applies.

A cheap invariant guard is worth adding regardless of root cause: OptimalPts should never be less than ActualPts, and RunLineupAnalysis could assert/clamp with a logged warning. A silent positive gap is the failure mode that let this sit unnoticed -- it renders on the dashboard as a green-looking day rather than an error.
acceptance_criteria: No date in the Lineup Gap Store has Gap > 0. The 2026-07-02 discrepancy is explained and either fixed or documented as a legitimate edge case with the invariant guard in place.
notes:
Found 2026-07-31 while backfilling the Lineup Gap Store for rosterbot-aei (grade --dates 2026-06-16:2026-07-27, exit 0). 1 of 45 days affected. Separately confirmed NOT related to rosterbot-i52: that backfill run logged '3 flagged, 0 resolved, 3 no-game, 0 failed' -- zero statsapi failures, because grade does one contiguous DailyFantasyPoints walk rather than recap-site's overlapping week-by-week re-walks. Also benign and NOT a bug: 2026-07-13/14/15 have actual=optimal=0 (All-Star break, no games).

=== ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-03) ===
None of the three causes hypothesised above. internal/backtest reuses the LIVE lineup optimizer as a HINDSIGHT engine. optimizer.optimalAssignment fills every slot it can and only leaves one empty when NO eligible player remains (the 'if !filled' branch) — sound when values are projections, which are never negative, and wrong when they are realised FPts, which go negative.

2026-07-02 evidence: only two pitchers had games against six P slots, so the optimizer ACTIVATED Roki Sasaki — a RESERVE who scored -9.00 — into a free slot. Pitcher optimal = 25 + (-9) = 16. Hitters lost another point the same way (Jake Bauers, -1, forced into a slot; true hitter max 26, computed 25). 25 + 16 = 41 vs actual 48 = Gap +7.

=== FIX ===
hindsightValue floors each player at max(0, FPts), applied in both hindsight sources at construction. Benching a player yields exactly 0 and that option is always available, so the floor IS the achievable optimum — and it makes optimal >= actual provable (the actual lineup's floored value is >= its raw value, and optimal dominates every feasible assignment). Deliberately NOT fixed in optimalAssignment: letting it choose empty slots would change live tie-breaks (equal-value empty branches grow ToBench and churn the roster, against the documented idempotency invariants) and slow the backtracking search. guardOptimal clamps any residual violation to actual with a stderr warning so a future regression surfaces instead of rendering green.

=== IMPACT (larger than the one reported day) ===
2026-06-16..07-27: 13 of 42 days had understated optima; positive-gap days 1 -> 0; efficiency 76.2% -> 74.6%. Full season 2026-03-26..08-02 (130 days): zero positive gaps. Actual points unchanged throughout — only the optimal side moved.

=== VERIFICATION ===
Lineup Gap Store backfilled 2026-06-16..2026-08-02 (48 days, also filling the 07-31..08-02 hole left by the STALE_CLIENT outage): positive_gap_days=0, efficiency 74.8%. Tests: two synthetic cases (negative reserve pulled into an empty slot; negative starter excluded), a guardOptimal table test incl. a float-noise case that must not clamp, and the real 2026-07-02 roster as internal/backtest/testdata/day-2026-07-02.json asserting optimal 51 / gap -3.

Follow-ups filed: rosterbot-bqf (negative bench FPts render as 'points left on bench'), rosterbot-n30 (grade --window 3 self-heals a shorter span than the outage that triggers escalation).
close_reason: Fixed in 6840f80 (PR #97): hindsight source floors player value at max(0, FPts). Verified zero positive gaps across the full season (130 days) and in the backfilled Lineup Gap Store (48 days, 2026-06-16..08-02).

title: MLB statsapi game-log backfill fails at ~80% during recap-site bulk rebuilds — leaves placeholder zeros in FPts
description:
During a full 'recap-site' build (observed in make run-all, 2026-07-31, 19 weeks), the MLB statsapi game-log backfill fails on the large majority of flagged rows in the early/bulk weeks and recovers only as the per-week volume thins:

  mlb backfill: 85 flagged,  5 resolved, 12 no-game, 68 failed
  mlb backfill: 66 flagged,  7 resolved, 34 no-game, 25 failed
  mlb backfill: 55 flagged,  2 resolved, 53 no-game,  0 failed
  mlb backfill: 57 flagged,  7 resolved, 49 no-game,  1 failed

The clustering (heavy failures early, zero once volume drops) is the signature of upstream rate-limiting / throttling from statsapi.mlb.com under back-to-back week builds, not of a logic error.

WHY THIS IS A CORRECTNESS ISSUE, NOT JUST NOISE. backfillDailyFPts (internal/fantrax/mlb_backfill.go) exists to resolve DayPlayerFP.needsBackfill rows -- players seen for the first time in the window, and two-way role crossings -- whose (deltaFP, deltaGP) were zeroed so pre-window cumulative YTD doesn't leak in as same-day production. It soft-fails to 'leave zero' on any error. So a failed backfill silently leaves the placeholder zero standing, deflating that player-day's FPts.

That is the same wrong number rosterbot-8ue fixed, arriving by a different route: 8ue fixed CALLERS FORGETTING to run the backfill (recap.seasonToDateTeamMean silently didn't), by folding it into DailyFantasyPoints. This is the backfill being called correctly and FAILING. Both deflate recap team totals and seasonToDateTeamMean, which is the WP-model input.

NOT A DUPLICATE OF rosterbot-qoa. qoa is about pastPeriodTTL=30d (internal/fantrax/cached.go:23) expiring immutable FANTRAX per-period snapshots, causing Monday refetches and superlinear recap-site runtime. This is a different cache and a different upstream: mlbBackfillGameLogTTL = time.Hour (internal/fantrax/mlb_backfill.go:23) governs the MLB game-log entries. Fixing qoa (infinite TTL for tierPast) would NOT remove this -- the 1h game-log TTL means every recap-site run re-fetches every game log regardless. The two share a trigger (recap-site rebuilding all weeks) and nothing else.
design:
Two candidate directions, not mutually exclusive:

1. Raise mlbBackfillGameLogTTL. A completed game's box score is immutable, so a 1h TTL on a PAST date is indefensible -- it is the same class of mistake as qoa's 30d TTL on immutable period snapshots. Date-aware TTL (long for past dates, short for today) removes most of the request volume outright and is likely the highest-value fix.

2. Add throttle/retry to the backfill fetch. pitcher_starts.go:107 already carries a 200ms/day throttle for the Fantrax side; the statsapi backfill has no equivalent. A retry with backoff on 429/5xx would convert transient throttling into a slower success rather than a silent zero.

Also worth deciding: whether a failed backfill should stay silent. It currently soft-fails by design so a recap render never breaks, which is right -- but a run that leaves 68 unresolved zeros should probably surface that count as a warning rather than an info line, since the resulting totals are known-wrong.
acceptance_criteria: A full recap-site build resolves backfills at a rate comparable to the thin-volume weeks (near-zero failures), or fails loudly enough that a run producing known-deflated totals is visible. Verify by counting 'failed' across a cold-cache 'make clean-cache && make run-all'.
notes:
UPDATE 2026-07-31, after rosterbot-qoa merged (commit 44a8029).

qoa's prediction held exactly: fixing the Fantrax snapshot TTL does NOT touch this. Measured on a settled week (2026-05-04:05-10) run twice back-to-back:

  cold: 57.8s   mlb backfill: 69 flagged, 10 resolved, 58 no-game, 1 failed
  warm:  2.8s   mlb backfill: 69 flagged, 10 resolved, 58 no-game, 1 failed

Identical backfill line both runs — the 1h mlbBackfillGameLogTTL re-fetches every game log on every run, exactly as this ticket says. Rendered HTML was byte-identical, so the warm run reproduced the cold run's backfill result rather than degrading.

WHAT CHANGED FOR THIS TICKET: this is now the dominant remaining per-week cost of a recap-site rebuild, and the only remaining source of superlinear-ish load on a bulk build. The Fantrax side is now a no-op on warm runs (permanent cache), so a full recap-site build's statsapi volume is no longer diluted by slow Fantrax round-trips — the game-log fetches will arrive back-to-back and FASTER than when this was filed. If the failure mode really is upstream throttling, removing the Fantrax pacing may make it WORSE, not better. Worth re-measuring a full `recap-site` build before choosing a fix.

Note the shape of the fix qoa used, since the same reasoning applies here: MLB game logs for a past date are immutable too, so the honest fix is a long/unbounded TTL plus (a) a volatility guard so today's log isn't pinned mid-game and (b) a season-scoped key. See internal/fantrax/cached.go PastPeriodTTL for the two invariants written out.

--- DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-11 (live, reproduced) ---

ROOT CAUSE IS NOT THROTTLING — throttling is only the TRIGGER. fetchAndResolve
(internal/playername/resolve.go) never returns an error: the per-batch
People.Search failure does `return nil` and the People.List failure does
`continue`. cache.Get caches whenever fetch() returns nil error
(internal/cache/cache.go:56), so a transient blip is written to disk and served
as authoritative for 7 days (cacheTTL = 7*24h). That is what converts a ~150ms
upstream hiccup into a week-long deterministic wrong answer with no signal.

Production evidence: 3 cached mlb-player-ids-* entries with ZERO resolved
players, all written in the 2026-07-31T08 bulk-build hour. That hour also wrote
186 of the 210 total resolver cache entries — the input-set-hash key gives near
zero reuse, which is the request volume that makes blips likely.

Live reproduction: first run of ResolveMLBAMIDsNoCache over 133 real Fantrax
names dropped 97; all 97 resolved individually. Three immediately following runs:
129/133 every time, 151-464ms. So the drop is real and transient, NOT
deterministic — the defect is the caching of it, not its occurrence.

SECOND DEFECT — search is sent the RAW name while dedup/matching use the
normalized one. Measured against MLB:
  "A.J. Blubaugh" raw=0 norm("aj blubaugh")=1
  "T.J. Rumfield" raw=0 norm=1
  "Zach Cole Jr." raw=0 norm=2
  "Ha-Seong Kim"  raw=1 norm("ha seong kim")=0
Neither form is a superset — hyphens need raw, periods/suffixes need normalized.
Fix is raw-first with a normalized retry for misses only.

LATENT HAZARD: go-mlb's WithNames joins the batch into one comma-delimited
`names` param (go-mlb@v0.1.2/options.go:363). Any raw name containing a comma —
the "Guerrero, Jr." form Normalize explicitly handles — splits the batch and
corrupts that request.

THIRD DEFECT — backfillDailyFPts increments the same failedCount for "no MLBAM
ID" and "game-log fetch failed", so the log line this ticket was filed from
could not have distinguished them. That is why the throttling read looked
supported.

NOT the fix: an external reference (Baseball Reference). 3 of the 4 genuine
misses are self-inflicted string handling. Only "Jake Latz" -> MLB's
"Jacob Latz" is a real identity gap.

SPUN OFF: rosterbot-bms (P1) — the same resolver silently returns the WRONG
player for namesakes (Jose Altuve -> a retired catcher). More severe than these
zeros and affects 5 call sites. rosterbot-txw — Sleeper parity exploration.

AGREED FIX (2026-08-11): retry failed batches with backoff, then refuse to cache
a degraded result; raw/normalized search fallback; split the failure counters.
close_reason: Root cause was not throttling — throttling was only the trigger. fetchAndResolve never returned an error, so cache.Get persisted partial/empty results for the full 7-day TTL, converting a ~150ms blip into a week-long wrong answer. Fixed all three defects: (1) per-batch retry with backoff, and a resolution that still fails returns errDegraded so the partial map is used for the run but never cached; (2) search now sends the raw name first and the normalized form only for misses, since neither is a superset (A.J. Blubaugh/Zach Cole Jr. need normalized, Ha-Seong Kim needs raw); (3) backfillDailyFPts splits Unresolved from FetchFailed and reports the last fetch error, so the log line can finally distinguish a poisoned resolution from an upstream outage — the missing evidence that let the throttling hypothesis stand untested. Verified live 2026-08-12: unresolvable names 4 -> 1 over a 133-name set. Residual is Jake Latz -> MLB's Jacob Latz, a legal/nickname gap no string transform closes; rosterbot-txw tracks whether Sleeper covers it.

title: Verify Projections tab renders correctly in a browser (rosterbot-aei follow-up)
description:
rosterbot-aei shipped web/dashboard/projections.js +197 lines (Decision quality headline block, rho tiles, gap chart, two-stacked-table compare under role All, Calibration diagnostics section) with NO browser verification. This repo has no JS test harness -- value.js, views.js, infra.js all ship untested -- so the change was verified by node --check plus hand-matching every Go JSON tag against every JS read site against real generated model.json/gap.json.

Residual risk the final review named: Chart.js runtime behaviour with empty datasets is untested against the real library, and all visual/layout concerns (light/dark, 390px mobile) are unchecked.

Check: headline block renders 4 tiles with real data and degrades to rho-only + 'no lineup gap data yet' when gap.json 404s; window toggle updates gap and rho together; role All shows two stacked compare tables; MAE tile shows the skill percentage under Calibration diagnostics; no console errors; light + dark + 390px.
design: Run 'rosterbot serve --web' locally (dashboard is passkey-gated, so local serve is the path) after seeding .analysis/ from s3://infrastack-statebucket446e0578-rm3scvdxnnyg/analysis/grades/ and .lineupgap/ via 'env -u STATE_BUCKET go run . grade --window 3'. Screenshot each state. Separately confirm against the deployed dashboard once ProjectionSite has run post-merge.
acceptance_criteria: Screenshots of the Projections tab in light and dark at desktop and 390px, with and without gap.json present, and a clean browser console.
notes:
2026-07-31 VERIFIED via screenshot (30d/All): tiles match model.json exactly — bench -87.0/3d, eff 79.4% (335/422), hitter +0.090 ±0.039 18/26, pitcher +0.384 ±0.108 12/15. Two rho tiles under role All (never pooled) confirmed. Two stacked comparison tables under All confirmed. 'Too close to call — no system leads by more than the combined standard error' rendering under Hitters, correctly refusing to crown steamer +0.127±0.040 over prod depthcharts +0.090±0.039. MAE spans only 4.30-4.41 across all four systems in that same table, which is the whole argument for the change visible in one row. STILL UNVERIFIED: dark mode, 390px mobile, empty-gap 404 state, browser console.
2026-08-11 VERIFIED end-to-end via a temporary local harness (web/dashboard/_verify.html, not committed — deleted after use). Environment note: the automated browser here has no WebAuthn platform authenticator, so the real login/bootstrap ceremony can't complete (register/begin succeeds 200, navigator.credentials.create() throws client-side, confirmed via network+console). Worked around by serving web/dashboard directly and importing projections.js's renderProjections() straight onto #view-root against the REAL production report/*.json pulled from s3://infrastack-dashboardbucket5758873d-4uhryuo4jsqe/report/ (same bytes CloudFront serves) — exercises the real Chart.js, api.js, render.js, same DOM, just skips the passkey shell.

Checked and passing: light+dark at desktop (1280) and 390px mobile; gap.json-404 degrade (mocked via fetch override at the harness level, since the Go static server's response wasn't reliably cache-busted through the browser) — headline correctly drops to rho-only tiles + "no lineup gap data yet", chart area empty, no console errors; window toggle (30d<->Season) updates gap chart + all 4 tiles + compare tables together; role toggle (All<->Hitters) correctly switches from two stacked compare tables to one; "too close to call" note renders correctly on both hitters/pitchers tables; all 5 chart types paint (gap bar, compare MAE-trend, detail trend, position bar, calibration scatter) — first paint can lag ~1s behind DOM insert (Chart.js async), not a bug, just don't screenshot at t=0. Console clean throughout (only two stale 401/404 entries left over from the pre-harness passkey-bootstrap attempt, unrelated to Projections).

BUG FOUND + FIXED (web/dashboard/style.css): the system-comparison/position/misses tables (6 cols incl. "±SE" spans) have no horizontal-scroll boundary, so at 390px their overflow bubbled up through <main> to <body>, widening the whole page's effective layout viewport to 463px (measured via scrollWidth/clientWidth/innerWidth) instead of just scrolling the table — a real "page scrolls sideways" bug. Fixed by scoping `overflow-x:auto` to the three table containers ([data-ref="compareTable"|"posTable"|"missTable"]). Verified fix: docScrollWidth==docClientWidth==390 after. Committed as 9fac469.

Same data-table class (no scroll wrapper) is used on Value/Trades/Runs tabs (web/dashboard/value.js, trades.js, runs.js, render.js) — likely the same bug there, out of scope for this ticket, flagged separately.

Remaining from the acceptance criteria: no actual screenshot files were saved/attached (this session has no artifact-attachment path to bd); the verification was interactive+scripted (DOM/scrollWidth assertions + visual screenshots reviewed in-session) rather than producing a checked-in image set. Deployed-dashboard confirmation (the DESIGN section's second step, "against the deployed dashboard once ProjectionSite has run post-merge") was not done since this session verified directly against production report/*.json rather than the deployed SPA.
close_reason: Verified via a local harness against real production report/*.json (WebAuthn can't run headlessly here, so login was bypassed at the DOM level, not the real network path). Light/dark x desktop/390px, gap.json-404 degrade, window/role toggles, and console cleanliness all checked and passing. Found and fixed a real mobile horizontal-scroll bug (page-level overflow from unbounded data-table width) — commit 9fac469. Same bug flagged separately for Value/Trades/Runs tabs (task_2bcf75df). Deployed-dashboard confirmation deferred to next ProjectionSite run post-merge, per the ticket's own design.

title: GS gate: fractional tail mixes value with count, and certaintyMargin is an order of magnitude too small
description: internal/optimizer/gs_budget.go. (1) Units: at :196 the fractional tail entry is 'placeholder * weight' where weight is a fractional COUNT (<=1), making it an expectation (value x probability), while every other entry in the ranking is a per-start value in points — and the cut at :224 spends a WHOLE slot on it. The trigger at :130 counts estimated demand fractionally but the allocation spends whole slots, so the fractional tail systematically loses the cut and future demand is under-reserved. This is an overcorrection of an earlier bug where the tail was ceil-rounded to full value; the fix swung past the target. Correct form is to keep the entry at full placeholder value and make the budget fractional, or to use one fractional currency throughout. (2) certaintyMargin=0.10 at :171 requires an estimated future start to beat today's by only 10% before outranking it, but measured SP projection MAE is 10.4-13.8 FP/game against an SP projection mean around 12 — projection noise on a single start is ~100% of its mean, so a 10% haircut is an order of magnitude too tight to encode 'this start might not happen at all'. Together with rosterbot-abd, all three defects push the same direction: under-reserving budget for future starts. In a weekly-capped league that means spending GS on Monday/Tuesday arms and hitting the cap before a Saturday ace — same number of starts, worse ones. The value-ranked pooling design itself is correct and should be kept; only the estimation and pricing of future demand is wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Trigger and allocation use one consistent currency. certaintyMargin re-derived from measured SP projection dispersion rather than left at 0.10.
close_reason: NOT A BUG (PR #99, 34da92b). No behavior change; the derivation is now written into gs_budget.go so it doesn't get refiled. Defect (1): the fractional tail's 'placeholder * weight' is NOT a units error. The weight belongs in the price precisely BECAUSE the cut spends a whole slot — the gate's question is marginal (hold this slot or spend it today?), holding is worth placeholder*min(E,1) in expectation, spending is worth the starter's value with certainty, and those are the two quantities that must be comparable. Counterexample against the prescribed full-value form: 1 slot left, certain 8-pt start today, 0.2 expected future starts at a 12-pt placeholder — full-value pricing benches the 8 to hold a slot that materializes 20%% of the time (2.4 expected vs 8 certain), and weekly GS is use-it-or-lose-it so the other 80%% is burned, not banked. The issue is also internally inconsistent: a LARGER certaintyMargin makes estimated-future outrank today LESS often, which spends more budget today — the opposite of the under-reserving it groups with rosterbot-abd. Defect (2): re-deriving certaintyMargin from SP projection MAE does not hold — that dispersion is symmetric, and haircutting an unbiased estimate biases the ranking rather than de-risking it. What the margin actually prices is P(the estimated start never materializes); now documented, along with the fact that 0.10 is an unmeasured prior. Measuring it split out to rosterbot-xsm. Tests: TestApplyGSGate_EstimatedLadderPricesWholeUnitsFullAndTailMarginally pins both rungs (E=1.4 -> 12.0 and 4.8); verified discriminating by mutation (pricing the tail at full value fails it and TestApplyGSGate_FractionalEstimateDoesNotOverSuppressToday).

title: Hourly optimize is 64% no-op and 75% of applied moves are re-flips
description: Measured from all notification objects in the state bucket: 711 kind=lineup notifications originate from only 224 distinct run_ids out of 613 optimize runs, so ~36% of hourly runs change anything. Of the moves that do apply, ~75% are re-flips of a (target_date, player) pair already moved — Alec Bohm was flipped 32 times for target date 2026-07-21 alone, Ryan Jeffers 29, Taylor Ward 29. Only ~16% of notifications concern today; 84% are future-dated --matchup speculation that gets re-decided next hour. 14% of changes gain <0.5 projected pts and 19% gain <1.0, which is far inside the 4.38 hitter MAE — i.e. the bot is applying and notifying on differences it cannot actually resolve. The zeroGainEps=1e-9 guard only catches exactly-zero gain.
design: Two changes, both cheap: (a) a real minimum-gain threshold (~1.0-1.5 projected pts, inside measured MAE) instead of zeroGainEps; (b) restrict the hourly loop to today only, and run the --matchup future pass once daily. Today is the only thing an hourly cadence can legitimately learn new information about (scratches, probables); re-deciding Saturday's lineup every hour on Tuesday is pure churn.
acceptance_criteria: Lineup churn and Pushover volume drop substantially without losing same-day late-scratch responsiveness.

comments.author: Jon Nixon
comments.text:
Root cause candidate found during the 2026-08-14 period-18 audit: rosterbot-6i4.

The premise that deltas are correct but too small does not hold. combinedMovesDelta (internal/lineuprun/display.go:30) credits the FULL pts of every entry in `activate`, and both optimizer paths put already-active players into ToActivate whenever only their SLOT changed (internal/optimizer/lineup.go:84, pitcher_lineup.go:159). A slot-changer never lands in `bench`, so nothing offsets the credit.

Measured: a PURE slot shuffle (two active players trading slots, nobody entering or leaving the lineup) reports +8.00 against a true gain of 0.00. A live case today reported +5.28 against a true +0.04.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S DESIGN: the proposed min-gain threshold of ~1.0-1.5 pts will NOT suppress these. Phantom gain is roughly one hitter's projected pts per shuffled player (~4.5), so a shuffle clears any threshold set inside hitter MAE. That is consistent with what this bead measured -- Bohm flipped 32 times for target date 2026-07-21, Jeffers 29, Ward 29 -- and with the 11-day delta distribution being bimodal (either <0.5, or clustered at ~4.5 / ~9 / ~13.5 / ~23, i.e. multiples of one hitter's pts) rather than continuous.

Part (b) of the design (restrict the hourly loop to today, run --matchup once daily) is unaffected and still stands on its own.

Suggest landing rosterbot-6i4 first, then re-measuring churn before choosing a threshold -- the residual after the fix may be much smaller than 14%/19% and would justify a different number. Marked as blocked-by 6i4.

title: System comparison ranks on unequal samples and pools LegacySystem into the incumbent
description: Two defects in internal/report make the dashboard's 'Best' system flag untrustworthy. (1) LegacySystem pooling: Aggregate attributes every empty-System row to detailSystem (depthcharts-ros). Verified from the raw store: LEGACY is MAE 4.8915 over n=298 across 14 days (2026-06-16..06-29, BEFORE any shadow system existed) while depthcharts-ros proper is MAE 4.9989 over n=552 across 27 days; pooling reports 4.9612. The incumbent is credited with 14 easier days no challenger was allowed to compete on, and on the true common window it ranks 3rd of 4 rather than 2nd. (2) rankSystems filters each system's rows independently and never intersects them, guarding only on N>0 — coverage is 40/25/25/22 days and n=827/509/509/439. A paired comparison on the 439-row intersection does show steamer-ros beating depthcharts-ros by 0.072 pts/player-day (p<0.001), but that is ~1.5% of MAE against within-day rank skill of +0.12, so it will flip almost no start/bench decisions. Do NOT switch production systems on this evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Compare/rankSystems inner-joins on (dt, player_id) across compared systems and reports the intersection N. LegacySystem rows are excluded from comparison (retained in detail Views for history). Best is set only when a paired test clears a minimum-N gate.

title: GS forecast caps pitcher count by slot count before dividing by rotation size
description: internal/lineuprun/gsbudget.go: the unannounced-day branch computes spPlaying (a count of rostered SPs whose team plays), caps it at numPSlots (a count of active pitcher SLOTS), then divides by rotationSize to get df.Estimated. The cap is applied to the wrong quantity — what is bounded by slot count is STARTS, not pitchers-whose-team-plays. Correct form is min(spPlaying/rotationSize, numPSlots). The branch immediately above it caps df.ConfirmedStarters at numPSlots, which IS correct because those are already starts — the contrast makes the unit error clear. Measured against the real roster (10 rostered SPs, 6 active pitcher slots): at 7 SPs playing Estimated=1.20 vs correct 1.40; at 8, 1.20 vs 1.60; at 10, 1.20 vs 2.00. With 10 rostered SPs the cap binds nearly every day, understating each unannounced day by 0.2-0.8 starts.
acceptance_criteria: Estimated future starts are not understated when more rostered SPs have a game than there are pitcher slots. Unit test covering spPlaying > numPSlots.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #98 (45d9fd7): min(spPlaying/rotationSize, numPSlots) — slot cap applies to starts, after the rotation divisor, not to the pitcher count before it. Regression test TestBuildGSForecast_MoreSPsPlayingThanSlotsDoesNotUnderstate (7 SPs playing / 6 slots = 1.4, fails at 1.2 on old code); the pre-existing TestBuildGSForecast_EstimateCapsAtActivePitcherSlots had pinned the bug (asserted 2/5=0.4) and was corrected to min(20/5,2)=2.0. CLAUDE.md GS-budget section now states the units.

title: Recap site viewership metrics: who is reading the weekly recap and how much
description:
No visibility into whether anyone reads the weekly recap. The recap site is built by recap-site into dist/, synced to SITE_BUCKET, and served by the SiteCdn CloudFront distribution (infra/infra.go). It is fully public: no auth, no signed URLs, no viewer-request function -- and CloudFront access logging is NOT enabled on the distribution today, so there is currently no signal at all, not even raw hits.

Scope is the recap site ONLY. The dashboard SPA and the lineup API are explicitly out of scope.

Want to answer: is anyone opening the weekly recap, which weeks get read (just the latest, or do people browse back through week-NN.html), and does readership hold up over the season or decay after the novelty. That last one is the decision this feeds: recap-site rebuilds every completed week on a schedule, and if nobody is reading it that cost is not justified.

Constraint that shapes everything: the page is public and the audience is a ~12-person league sharing one link. There is no login to attribute a view to, so 'who' is not directly answerable the way it would be on the passkey-gated dashboard.
design:
DECIDED 2026-07-27. Two steps; step 1 is shipped in PR #91.

STEP 1 (done, PR #91): enable CloudFront standard logging on SiteCdn -> RecapLogBucket under recap/, 90-day expiry, ObjectOwnership=OBJECT_WRITER (CloudFront logs via ACL; the CDK default silently yields no logs). Glue table rosterbot_analysis.recap_access_logs for ad-hoc queries. DashboardCdn deliberately not logged.

STEP 2 (this issue, blocked on step 1 being DEPLOYED so real log objects exist): surface it on the dashboard SPA.

  Data path -- read the log objects from S3 directly. NOT Athena. A pure aggregator walks the recap/ prefix with internal/s3blob (Walk + Get, from rosterbot-oye), gunzips, parses the TSV, and produces a Model. This matches internal/report and internal/valuereport exactly -- pure aggregation, no I/O in the domain package, serialized straight to JSON. Athena was rejected: it adds the Athena SDK, async submit/poll, and reading results back out of S3 -- three independently-failing moving parts for a dataset small enough to read whole. The 90-day lifecycle rule bounds the scan for free.

  Content -- a RECENT HITS TABLE only. Columns: timestamp (log_date + log_time, UTC), client IP, page (uri_stem), edge location. This is the literal ask -- when, and from what IP. Explicitly NOT building: views-over-time chart, per-week-page breakdown, distinct-readers-per-day. Do not add them speculatively.

  Wiring -- follow the model.json/value.json path exactly: written by projection-site (or its own command) to ./report/views.json, synced by entrypoint.sh under DASHBOARD_BUCKET's report/ prefix, fetched client-side by a new SPA tab. Soft-fail independently like renderValueSite does, so a log-parsing hiccup never blocks the accuracy dashboard deploy.

  Filtering -- restrict to real page reads (status 200, uri_stem LIKE '%.html') so CSS/asset/favicon requests do not drown the table. CloudFront logs every object, not every page view.

  Geolocation -- edge_location only (the POP that served the request, e.g. SFO5 -> rough metro). Standard logs carry no country field; real geo needs standard logging v2 or an IP->geo lookup. Confirmed nice-to-have, not required. Do not add a dependency for it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A dashboard SPA tab shows a recent-hits table for the recap site: timestamp, client IP, page, edge location.
2. Rows are real page reads -- status 200 and .html only, not every asset request.
3. views.json is produced by a pure aggregator with no I/O in the domain package, reading log objects via internal/s3blob; no Athena SDK dependency is added.
4. A failure to read or parse logs soft-fails and does not block model.json/value.json publication.
5. Empty state renders cleanly -- a freshly deployed log prefix has no objects, and the tab must not error on that.
6. Documented in CLAUDE.md alongside the other dashboard/report sections.
notes:
Step 1 shipped as PR #91 (branch feat/recap-access-logs) on 2026-07-27; NOT yet merged/deployed at time of writing. Step 2 is blocked until it deploys and real log objects accumulate -- building the renderer against an empty prefix means 'verifying' it against nothing.

Also depends on rosterbot-oye (PR #90) merging, since the aggregator reads via internal/s3blob.

Scope was narrowed twice by the user: first from three surfaces (dashboard SPA + recap site + lineup API) to the recap site ONLY, then from four candidate visualizations to the recent-hits table ONLY.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #91 (ed881cb: CloudFront standard logging on SiteCdn -> RecapLogBucket under recap/, 90-day expiry, Glue table) and PR #92 (dcdfd8b: Views tab + internal/recaplog aggregator), both merged to main. All 6 acceptance criteria verified against main: (1) web/dashboard/views.js renders the recent-hits table, tab wired at index.html:38; (2) recaplog.IsPageRead filters to status 200 + / or *.html; (3) pure aggregator reading via internal/s3blob, no Athena SDK in go.mod; (4) renderViewsSite soft-fails with a warning (cmd/projection-site.go:87) and never blocks model.json/value.json; (5) empty prefix renders 'No page reads recorded yet.' (views.js:98); (6) CLAUDE.md documents internal/recaplog. go test ./internal/recaplog/... passes.

title: Infra tab: AWS data-state status page on the dashboard
description:
Add an 'Infra' tab to the dashboard SPA (web/dashboard/) showing the health and freshness of every durable and ephemeral data artifact in AWS, so "is anything quietly broken?" is one glance instead of an S3 spelunk.

TODAY there is no way to see this. The Jobs and Runs tabs answer "did the job run?" — they read the run ledger. They do NOT answer "did the job produce data, and is that data still arriving?" A job can exit 0 having written nothing, and nothing surfaces it. Two failure modes make that more than cosmetic:

1. The Team Value Store ACCUMULATES FORWARD AND CANNOT BE BACKFILLED (docs/adr/0002). HKB has no history and rosters are not archived, so a day missed is permanently lost. A silent gap in analysis/team-values/dt=* is unrecoverable data loss that currently nobody would notice until the Value tab's chart looked wrong.
2. The Analysis Store partitions by dt AND system (4 shadow systems). A shadow capture that silently stops for one system degrades the model-comparison ranking without any error anywhere.

WHAT TO SURFACE — every artifact, its last-written partition/date, its age, and a health verdict:

  Durable (S3, keep-forever):
    analysis/grades/dt=*/system=*   Analysis Store — last dt, size, and WHICH of the 4 systems reported (a missing system is the interesting case)
    analysis/team-values/dt=*       Team Value Store — last dt + GAP DETECTION across the series (see above; gaps are permanent)
    archive/<source>/dt=*           daily raw-data archive — per source: hkb, fangraphs (4 systems x bat/pit = 8 blobs), savant (5 CSVs), prospects
    backtest/snapshots/             flat per-day projection snapshots (what the "backtest" command grades)
    backtest/snapshots-systems/     per-system shadow captures
    runledger/, runs/, notifications/, lineup/, claims/, session/

  Ephemeral (TTL-evicted, regenerable):
    cache/                          total size, object count, and age distribution by TTL tier (todayTTL 15m / stableTTL 7d / pastPeriodTTL 30d) — plus the provider-specific ones: fangraphs 24h, savant 24h, hkb 8h, prospect-rankings 168h

  Producers: map each artifact to the EventBridge schedule that writes it (Lineup, Prospects, GsCheck, Waivers, Transactions, Claims, Backtest, Grade, ProjectionSite, Archive, TeamValues, Shadow) so a stale artifact points at a suspect job.
design:
TWO PLAUSIBLE DATA PATHS — pick deliberately, they have different properties:

  (a) PRECOMPUTED JSON, like the existing Projections and Value tabs. A command (extend the "projection-site" command, or add a new "infra-status" one) walks the prefixes, writes report/infra.json under DASHBOARD_BUCKET, and infra.js fetches it. Cheap, no new IAM, no new API surface, matches the two newest tabs. But it is only as fresh as its last scheduled run — a real weakness for a page whose entire job is detecting staleness. A status page that is itself stale can report "all healthy" while the producer that writes it is the thing that died.

  (b) LIVE API, like Jobs/Runs. New GET /v1/infra route in internal/lineupapi doing the S3 listing on demand. Always current, and it can honestly report its own failure. Costs a new route, Lambda S3 list permissions across the prefixes, and latency (many ListObjectsV2 calls) — mitigable with a short server-side cache.

RECOMMEND (b) for correctness of purpose, with a small TTL. If (a) is chosen for expedience, the page MUST prominently display the generated-at timestamp of infra.json itself and go red when that is stale — otherwise the page can lie in exactly the situation it exists to catch.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- Prefix layout is already centralized in internal/statestore (artifact{s3Prefix, localDir}). Read it from there; do NOT hardcode a second copy of the prefix table — that is precisely what rosterbot-9s6 collapsed.
- Prefer S3 ListObjectsV2 with delimiter to enumerate dt= partitions without fetching objects. Row counts, if shown, need object reads — consider showing object SIZE instead, which listing gives free.
- Health thresholds should be per-artifact, not global: cache/ being 15 minutes old is healthy; analysis/team-values/ being 2 days old is not. Encode the expected cadence per artifact alongside the prefix.
- Follow the existing SPA conventions: add a route to ROUTES in app.js, a nav anchor href="#infra" in index.html, and an infra.js exporting renderInfra(root). Vendored Chart.js is already available if a sparkline of arrival history is wanted.
- The dashboard is passkey-gated; the precomputed JSON files are NOT (documented in docs/aws-deployment.md). If (a) is chosen, infra.json inherits that same public-by-URL exposure — check nothing sensitive (bucket names, ARNs, account IDs) lands in it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An 'Infra' tab exists in the dashboard nav and routes to a rendered view.
2. Every durable prefix and the ephemeral cache are listed with last-written date, age, and a health verdict.
3. Team Value Store gap detection is present and calls out missing days explicitly — this is the artifact that cannot be backfilled.
4. Analysis Store shows per-system coverage, so one shadow system silently stopping is visible.
5. Archive shows per-source freshness (hkb / fangraphs / savant / prospects), not one aggregate.
6. Each artifact names the EventBridge schedule that produces it.
7. The page cannot silently present stale data as healthy: either it reads live, or it displays and alarms on its own generation timestamp.
8. Prefix layout is read from internal/statestore, not duplicated.
9. Works in both light and dark, and on a phone — this is a page to check from bed when a Pushover fires.
notes: Requested 2026-07-25. Related: the Jobs and Runs tabs already cover run-level status via the run ledger; this is deliberately the DATA-level complement and should not duplicate them. Consider cross-linking a stale artifact to its producer job's last run in the Runs tab.
close_reason: Shipped. PR #85, merged as 54359b2. GET /v1/infra + Infra dashboard tab, live S3 listing (not precomputed — a status page built from a scheduled artifact goes stale in exactly the situation it exists to detect). New zero-dep leaf internal/statestore/layout is now the single bucket-layout declaration (statestore imports lineupapi, so lineupapi could never import statestore back). 15 tests, all judgement logic testable without AWS. Gap detection scans only to yesterday (today's producer may not have run) and is fatal only where NoBackfill is set. Sub-dimension coverage surfaces a stopped shadow system as a missing chip. IAM = s3:ListBucket only, never GetObject. Verified live against local state: correctly flagged a 12-day-old Fantrax session cookie as stale. UI screenshotted light/dark/390px + synthetic gap fixture. Extra beyond issue scope: lineupapi.NewFileInfraStore so local serve shows the same view (needed to verify UI at all — SPA is passkey-gated).

title: Add a LICENSE to the public repo
description:
github.com/nixon-commits/rosterbot is PUBLIC and has NO license file (confirmed via gh repo view: visibility=PUBLIC, license=NONE). Under default copyright that means all rights reserved: nobody can legally fork, use, modify or contribute, even though the source is readable. Anyone who has already cloned it is technically in the wrong.

One-file fix that changes the repo's legal posture.
design:
The choice is the owner's call, not a default to be assumed. MIT is the usual pick for a personal project like this and is the least friction.

The repo vendors nothing but depends on github.com/pmurley/go-fantrax and the AWS SDK; neither appears to impose copyleft that would constrain the choice, but confirm before picking.

Add the file, then make sure GitHub picks it up so the license shows in the repo sidebar (it detects standard LICENSE filenames and contents automatically).
acceptance_criteria:
1. A LICENSE file exists at the repo root.
2. GitHub shows the license in the repo sidebar.
notes:
SCOPE REDUCED 2026-07-25: originally also proposed retiring docs/superpowers/ and docs/agents/. Owner decided to KEEP both — do not delete them.

One genuinely stale item was found during that survey and is worth a separate look someday, but is NOT part of this issue: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md describes issues living as markdown under .scratch/<feature-slug>/, a directory that does not exist (the repo uses beads now), and CLAUDE.md:227 still cites it as current. That is a doc-accuracy nit, not a deletion.
close_reason: Added GPL-3.0 LICENSE. NOTE: the issue's design assumption was wrong — go-fantrax (both pmurley upstream and the nixon-commits fork) is GPL-3.0 and is statically linked, so the combined work must be GPL-3.0; MIT was not available. Owner chose GPL-3.0 after being shown the finding. README gained a License section explaining the constraint.

title: Extract BlendSources phase: make projection blending pure and testable
description:
rosterbot-6rv criterion 3, remaining half. The GS-budget half landed in PR #84 (countTodayStarts pure, buildGSForecast behind a schedule seam, 8 tests). Projection blending did not.

Blending currently happens inline in lineuprun.Run across two blocks — the hitter section (~50 lines, windowedHitterRecent + BlendedSource wiring) and the pitcher section (~90 lines, GetRecentPitcherStats + PitcherBlendedSource). Neither is exercised by any test; windowedHitterRecent in particular reconstructs a per-day FPts series via DailyFantasyPoints over ~35 days and collapses it through projections.WindowedRecent + WindowWeight(30), and a mistake there silently shifts every hitter's Expected Points.

The issue's own design note calls this out: 'GSBudget and BlendSources should come out fully pure; that is where the real leverage is.'
design:
Mirror what worked for the GS-budget extraction: identify the genuinely pure core, put a narrow interface in front of the fetch, and inject anything expensive as a func value rather than passing a whole source.

The pure core is the collapse of a per-day FPts series into per-player FP/game + games-in-window. That should be a function taking the already-fetched []fantrax.DayRoster and returning the recent-stat map, with no client at all. The fetch (DailyFantasyPoints over the trailing window) stays behind the existing recentStatsClient seam.

Pitchers are simpler — GetRecentPitcherStats returns a YTD snapshot map directly — so the phase is mostly about lifting the BlendedSource/PitcherBlendedSource construction and its GP-threshold logic somewhere testable.

Both roles must keep their asymmetry: hitters use a trailing 30-day window (rosterbot-2nd), pitchers use season-to-date YTD. That asymmetry is deliberate and backtest-justified; do not unify it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Blending logic runs in tests with no network and no credentials.
2. The hitter window collapse is a pure function over already-fetched data.
3. Hitters stay on the 30-day window and pitchers on YTD — the rosterbot-2nd asymmetry is preserved and a test says so.
4. Dry-run output stays byte-identical (build a baseline binary from the pre-change commit; run back-to-back with identical stream redirection — live projections drift within the hour).
notes: Baseline-diff technique and its two gotchas are recorded on rosterbot-6rv.
close_reason: Closed

title: Declare a narrow Fantrax interface in lineuprun, recap and gscheck instead of taking the concrete 34-method client
description:
internal/fantrax.Client exposes 34 methods over roster fetch, period math, scoring config, lineup apply, stats/backfill, player pool, transactions and matchups, and embeds two concrete upstream types with no interface between them (client.go:188 -- public *gofantrax.Client, auth *auth_client.Client).

Three consumer packages take that concrete client as their entry-point parameter:
  internal/lineuprun/lineuprun.go:130   Run(ft *fantrax.Client, cfg *config.Config, opts Options)
  internal/recap/recap.go:32            Run(ft *fantrax.Client, opts Options)
  internal/recap/site.go:31             RunSite(ft *fantrax.Client, sopts SiteOptions)
  internal/recap/leaders.go:45          buildLeaders(ft *fantrax.Client, ...)
  internal/gscheck/gscheck.go:83        RunGSCheck(ft *fantrax.Client, cfg config.Config)

Three others already declare the narrow interface they actually use, and this issue is asking for nothing more than the same treatment:
  internal/waivers/types.go:42       FantraxClient (5 methods)
  internal/claims/types.go:12        ClaimsClient  (1 method)
  internal/transactions.go:20        TradeClient   (2 methods)

Test coverage tracks that split almost exactly. recap sits at ~50% -- awards.go, wp.go, standings_history.go and render.go (pure, view-model only) are well covered, while recap.go, site.go and leaders.go are at 0%. lineuprun has 5 tests covering pure helpers and none covering Run. gscheck orchestration is likewise unexercised.

These are the three packages with the documented period-drift incident history (rosterbot-uv6, rosterbot-z3b, rosterbot-2ax, rosterbot-48z): a false league-wide GS alert, an 11-day duplicate-notification flood, and a silent lineup-apply failure masked as success. None of those could have been caught by a package-level test, because there is no seam at which to inject a fake Fantrax.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 4 of 7).
design:
Consumer-side interfaces only -- internal/fantrax does not change, and *fantrax.Client keeps satisfying every new interface implicitly.

For each of the three packages, declare the minimal method set its entry point actually calls and take that instead of the concrete type. Precedent for shape and placement is internal/waivers/types.go:42 (a named interface in the consuming package, documented as isolated for testability).

Notes for the grilling pass:
  - recap is the largest surface: recap.go + site.go + leaders.go together touch rosters, matchups, daily FPts, pitcher starts, the player pool and GetScoringPeriodsAndTeams. Decide whether that is one interface or two (a week-aggregation interface and a leaders interface), guided by what a test actually needs to fake.
  - fantrax.WeekBounder (matchup_week_resolve.go:8) is the existing example of an interface declared in the fantrax package and consumed by backtest. Decide deliberately whether new interfaces follow that direction or the waivers direction (declared by the consumer). Consumer-declared is the Go idiom and keeps fantrax free of consumer concerns.
  - A fake is only worth building if tests are actually written against it -- one adapter is a hypothetical seam. This issue should land WITH at least one real orchestration test per package, not just the interface.
  - This unblocks the Lineup Run phase-split issue, whose phase-level tests need the same seam.
acceptance_criteria:
1. lineuprun.Run, recap.Run, recap.RunSite and gscheck.RunGSCheck take a package-declared interface rather than *fantrax.Client.
2. *fantrax.Client satisfies each new interface with no changes to internal/fantrax.
3. Each of the three packages gains at least one orchestration-level test driven by a fake implementing its interface -- not just leaf-helper tests.
4. At least one previously-uncatchable failure mode is covered by a new test (e.g. a period-resolution mismatch feeding the apply path, or recap season-mean aggregation).
5. Coverage for internal/recap and internal/gscheck measurably increases; recap.go / site.go / leaders.go are no longer at 0%.
6. go vet ./... and make test pass.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #79. Narrow Fantrax interfaces for gscheck/recap/lineuprun with fake-driven tests; fantrax untouched.

title: DailyFantasyPoints leaks NeedsBackfill to callers; recap seasonToDateTeamMean skips the backfill and undercounts
description:
internal/fantrax.DailyFantasyPoints (daily_fpts.go:70) zeroes a player deltaFP/deltaGP on first appearance in the window and on a two-way role crossing, flags the row NeedsBackfill (daily_fpts.go:34), and returns it as-is. Resolving those placeholders requires a SECOND, separate call to Client.BackfillDailyFPts (mlb_backfill.go:81), which fetches the MLB statsapi game log and scores it via the Scoring Weights.

That pairing is a convention, not an invariant. Six call sites exist; five remember it, one does not:

  PAIRED:   cmd/grade.go:65+69, cmd/backtest.go:96+100, cmd/backtest.go:172+176,
            internal/recap/recap.go:245+249, internal/lineuprun/recent.go:47+53
  UNPAIRED: internal/recap/recap.go:555 (seasonToDateTeamMean)

seasonToDateTeamMean fetches the full seasonStart..asOf window and hands the rows straight to computeSeasonMeanFromDays (recap.go:559), which cannot distinguish a placeholder zero from a genuine off-day. Every player whose first appearance falls mid-window -- i.e. every mid-season waiver pickup and every Ohtani-style role crossing -- contributes 0 FPts on that day, silently deflating the teams season-to-date daily mean. That mean feeds the recap win-probability model via fetchSeasonMeans, so the error propagates into the WP curves and Game of the Week pick.

This is the interface defect behind the bug: NeedsBackfill is an implementation detail (Fantrax YTD snapshot diffs cannot see a players first appearance) promoted onto the interface as a flag callers must remember to act on.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 3 of 7, top recommendation).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Pick a team that acquired a player via waivers or trade mid-season, and a week after that acquisition.
2. Run: go run . recap --dates <that week> --out /tmp/recap.html
3. Instrument or inspect seasonToDateTeamMean (internal/recap/recap.go:551) for that teamID -- note the DayPlayerFP rows where NeedsBackfill is true and FPts is 0.
4. Compare the returned mean against the same computation with ft.BackfillDailyFPts(days) inserted after recap.go:555.
5. The unpatched mean is lower; the gap scales with how many rostered players first appear mid-window.
design:
Deepen the module rather than adding a sixth reminder to call the pairing.

Move the backfill inside DailyFantasyPoints so the returned []DayRoster never contains placeholder zeros:
  - DailyFantasyPoints resolves NeedsBackfill rows internally before returning.
  - BackfillDailyFPts becomes unexported (backfillDailyFPts); the five paired call sites drop their explicit call and their error-handling block.
  - NeedsBackfill stays on the struct only if some caller genuinely needs to know a row was reconstructed rather than diffed; otherwise it becomes unexported too.

Error policy must be decided explicitly and documented on DailyFantasyPoints: the existing backfill soft-fails to leave-zero on any MLB statsapi error, and internal/lineuprun/recent.go:53 already discards the error outright (_ = ft.BackfillDailyFPts(days)). Preserve soft-fail so a statsapi hiccup never breaks a recap, but the behaviour belongs in the doc comment as part of the interface, not in five call sites.

Cost note: the backfill is bounded to a handful of statsapi calls per window and is already paid by five of six callers, so folding it in does not change the network profile of any existing paired path. seasonToDateTeamMean (a full-season window) is the one path that gains calls -- it is also the one currently producing wrong numbers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. internal/recap/recap.go:555 (seasonToDateTeamMean) no longer returns placeholder zeros for mid-window first appearances.
2. DailyFantasyPoints resolves the backfill internally; BackfillDailyFPts is no longer exported.
3. The five previously-paired call sites (grade.go, backtest.go x2, recap.go:245, recent.go) call DailyFantasyPoints alone and still produce identical output.
4. A unit test covers the mid-window-first-appearance case and the two-way role-crossing case through the DailyFantasyPoints interface (not through the unexported backfill).
5. The soft-fail-on-statsapi-error policy is documented on DailyFantasyPoints doc comment.
6. Recap totals still match the Fantrax-authoritative Matchup.HomeTeam.Points for a spot-checked week (the existing verification described in CLAUDE.md).
7. go vet ./... and make test pass; CLAUDE.md updated where it describes the DailyFantasyPoints/BackfillDailyFPts pairing.
close_reason: Folded MLB-statsapi backfill into DailyFantasyPoints; backfillDailyFPts + needsBackfill unexported; seasonToDateTeamMean (WP-model input) now backfills. Covered by TestDailyFantasyPoints_ResolvesBackfillInternally via a fetchPeriodSnapshotFn seam.

title: applyLineupWithLockedPlayerRetry trusts retry response instead of verifying the intended change landed
description: Discovered while diagnosing rosterbot-2ax's live drift (2026-07-16): applyLineupWithLockedPlayerRetry (internal/fantrax/apply_lineup.go) excludes the named locked players from the retry payload, then treats an empty/benign response as full success for the REMAINING (non-excluded) changes too, without verifying they actually landed. During the 2026-07-16 incident, the hourly Lineup job's retry excluded Lewis/Bohm (correctly locked, wrong-period side effect), got a benign response back, and logged 'Lineup applied successfully' for 3+ consecutive hourly runs — but the paired Jeffers/Alvarez swap (not itself named as locked) also silently failed to apply, and nothing detected it. Add a post-retry roster verification step (re-fetch the roster and confirm the non-excluded intended changes actually took effect) before declaring success, or at minimum log a clear warning when a retry's outcome can't be positively confirmed.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #62 (branch fix/rosterbot-48z-post-retry-verify): verifyExcludedRetry re-fetches roster after locked-player retry and confirms non-excluded changes landed; mismatch errors (log+Pushover), fetch-error soft-fails, clean apply skips verify. Re-close on main (original close was on the feature branch).

title: Unify Class-A period resolution (DailyPeriodFor/AnchorPeriodForDate) onto the authoritative periodList map
description: Follow-up to rosterbot-1i3/rosterbot-ren. The periodList date->daily-period map (DisplayedLists["periodList"] from getTeamRosterInfo, 187 entries spanning the season) is the authoritative source; rosterbot-ren wires it into the Class-B historical consumers (DailyFantasyPoints, GetTeamPitcherStarts). Class A (near-today, action-affecting) still uses the anchored DailyPeriodFor/AnchorPeriodForDate free functions for lineup-apply and GetTeamGS. Those produce identical results today (zero drift as of 2026-07-15) but are a second, guess-based resolution mechanism. Rebase them onto the same authoritative map so there is ONE source of period truth. Blast radius: DailyPeriodFor/AnchorPeriodForDate are pure free functions with no *Client, so threading the map in means signature changes plus gsPeriodWalk/gs_check/lineuprun call-site updates, and it touches the live lineup-apply hot path -- hence deferred out of the 1i3+ren PR.
close_reason: Fixed: DailyPeriodFor is now a *Client method that consults the authoritative periodDateMap before falling back to the anchor. Live drift confirmed and fix verified end-to-end on 2026-07-16 (branch fix/rosterbot-2ax-period-resolution). Follow-up filed as rosterbot-48z for the retry-masking gap this surfaced.

title: optimize: blank player names in lineup-change notifications for future dates
description:
## Symptom
Fantrax Lineup Pushover alerts for future dates (seen during the All-Star-break --matchup run, e.g. Jul 23/25/26) show pitcher/hitter moves with MISSING names — 'arrow -> P' and 'arrow -> BN' with no player name — while other moves render fine.

## Root cause
cmd/optimize.go builds the change-line name lookup (playerName map) ONCE from today's base roster (GetHitterRoster/GetPitcherRoster). But the per-date apply loop optimizes future dates against PERIOD-SPECIFIC rosters (GetHitterRosterForPeriod/GetPitcherRosterForPeriod), which can include players not on today's active roster (e.g. reserve/IL SPs surfaced for a matchup week). When the optimizer activates or benches such a player, playerName[id] is empty -> blank name in the notification. Verified live: today's base pitcher roster = 14, period rosters = 20; 8 pitcher IDs (Griffin Jax, Dennis Santana, Yusei Kikuchi, ...) are absent from the base map. Not merged-period-specific and not caused by the GS fix (rosterbot-wd5); a latent bug surfaced by multi-future-date --matchup optimization.

## Fix
Resolve change-line names from THIS date's result (dr.hitterResult/pitcherResult .Scored players carry the period-specific names), seeded from the global map for safety. Applied to both stdout change list and the Pushover summary. Live-verified: 2026-07-26 now shows 'Griffin Jax -> P', 'Dennis Santana -> P', etc.; also fixed blank '-> BN -0.00' cosmetic moves (Joey Wiemer, Julio Rodriguez).
acceptance_criteria: Future-date optimize runs render all activated/benched player names in stdout and Pushover output, including players present only in the period-specific roster. Live-verified for 2026-07-26 and 2026-07-28.
close_reason: Merged in PR #51 (commit ca41337) — change-line names now resolved from the period-specific optimizer result, live-verified for 2026-07-26/28.

title: Validate daily-period numbering across the All-Star break (period 16) for GS tally
description:
Follow-up to rosterbot-wd5. GetTeamGS/GetTeamPitcherStarts walk the merged 2-week ASB period (16, 2026-07-13..07-26) using daily anchor arithmetic, which assumes Fantrax's DAILY scoring periods advance one-per-calendar-day through the break. If Fantrax merges daily periods during the break (as it merges the WEEKLY matchup period), the anchor arithmetic drifts and the per-day snapshot diff could mis-attribute a start or two around the break boundary. Impact is small (few games during the break) but should be confirmed.

## What to do
Near/after 2026-07-27 (first gs-check of period 16), run the gs-check dry-run (or a probe) and confirm: (a) daily periods 111..124 actually map to 07-13..07-26 with no merges, and (b) the period-16 GS tallies are realistic. If daily periods DO merge across the break, the walk needs Fantrax's authoritative daily-period date map rather than pure anchor arithmetic — coordinate with the still-open rosterbot-ren (exact date→period map).
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed whether Fantrax daily periods merge across the ASB; period-16 GS tallies validated as correct, or a follow-up fix filed if they drift.
close_reason: Superseded by rosterbot-2ax (closed 2026-07-16). The ASB-drift risk this was meant to validate is structurally eliminated: gsPeriodWalk->DailyPeriodFor now resolves each day via the authoritative periodDateMap (Fantrax periodList date->daily-period dropdown) first, not pure anchor arithmetic — so any daily-period merge/insertion across the All-Star break is reflected automatically. Both deps (rosterbot-ren, rosterbot-2ax) landed. No manual 07-27 probe needed.

title: CDK: team-values EventBridge schedule (~14:00 UTC)
description:
Add an EventBridge schedule in infra/ (Go CDK) that runs the team-values command daily at ~14:00 UTC - after grade (13:30) and before projection-site (15:00) so the site renders today's point same-day.
