title: Board column drift: ❌ counted single-width but renders double-width
description:
internal/lineuprun/display.go's displayWidth treats every BMP rune as one terminal column and only U+10000+ as two. ❌ (U+274C, the real-life-benched marker) is BMP but renders double-width in most terminals, so any hitter row carrying it pushes the │ column separator one cell right.

Found while writing the render goldens for rosterbot-rr1; pre-existing, not introduced by that change. The goldens in internal/lineuprun/testdata/ currently lock in the misaligned output, so fixing this means regenerating them (go test ./internal/lineuprun/ -run TestRenderDateResult -update) and reading the diff.
design:
Either add the handful of BMP double-width ranges displayWidth actually needs (the emoji-presentation blocks around U+2600-27BF plus the U+FE0F variation selector), or take the dependency on golang.org/x/text/width / mattn/go-runewidth and delete the hand-rolled function. The second is more correct and the tree already pulls golang.org/x/*; the first avoids a dep for one glyph.

Check the other non-ASCII markers the board uses at the same time: ▸ ✓ ★ · ─ ═ ║ ╔ are all single-width, 🔒 is correctly detected.
acceptance_criteria: A hitter row with ❌ aligns its column separator with every other row; goldens regenerated and the diff shows only the intended shift.
close_reason: displayWidth now measures East Asian Width via golang.org/x/text/width (Wide/Fullwidth=2, Ambiguous=1). ❌ (U+274C) counts 2; box-drawing/★/✓/▸ stay 1. Goldens regenerated — diff is one space removed on the single ❌ row in each. Added TestDisplayWidth + TestPadRight_DoubleWidthMarker.

title: Thread BACKTEST_ARCHIVE env read through lineuprun.Options like Publisher
description: internal/lineuprun/lineuprun.go:948 reads os.Getenv("BACKTEST_ARCHIVE")=="1" inline (a back-compat snapshot-archival alias for --archive-projections). This is the same anti-pattern rosterbot-9s6 removed for STATE_BUCKET: an orchestration package reading a config env var directly instead of receiving it from cmd. Options already has ArchiveProjections bool; cmd should resolve BACKTEST_ARCHIVE and OR it into that field (or a dedicated Options field), leaving lineuprun free of os.Getenv entirely. Out of scope for 9s6 (which targeted STATE_BUCKET store selection); surfaced during 9s6 Task 4. Low priority — behavior is correct today.
close_reason: Done by rosterbot-6rv criterion 5 (PR #84, commit c996e24). cmd.resolveWriteSnapshots now folds BACKTEST_ARCHIVE=1, --snapshot, --archive-projections and the dry-run default into a single Options.WriteSnapshots bool, resolved at the flag layer. internal/lineuprun contains zero os.Getenv calls. Went further than this issue proposed: rather than OR-ing the env var into the existing ArchiveProjections field, the three redundant snapshot fields (SnapshotFlag/ArchiveProjections/ForceSnapshot) collapsed into one resolved decision. 8 table cases pin the deprecated aliases, including that only the exact value '1' enables the env var.

title: Delete the pass-through NDJSON store wrappers and share one S3 blob adapter
description:
Lowest-payoff candidate of the seven from the 2026-07-22 architecture review -- filed for tracking, not as a recommendation to act soon.

Two separate observations, both about plumbing left over after the internal/ndjsonstore extraction.

(a) Shallow wrappers. internal/analysis and internal/teamvalue each expose a Writer interface + writer struct + two constructors, and a Reader interface + reader struct + two constructors -- eight constructors total across the two packages -- whose bodies forward exactly one call:

    analysis/grades.go:82   func (w writer) WriteGrades(date, system, rows) error {
                              return ndjsonstore.Write(w.store, objectKey(date, system), rows)
                            }
    analysis/reader.go:12   reader -> ndjsonstore.ReadAll with a decorate hook
    teamvalue/teamvalue.go, teamvalue/reader.go -- same shape, minus the system dimension

Deletion test: remove analysis.Writer and have callers hold an ndjsonstore.Store and call ndjsonstore.Write(store, analysis.ObjectKey(date, system), rows) directly -- no complexity reappears. The row type (GradeRow / Row), the partition-key logic (ObjectKey, SystemFromKey, LegacySystem) and the decorate hook DO earn their keep and must stay; only the wrapper indirection is shallow.

ndjsonstore itself is deep and should not be touched: Marshal/Unmarshal/Write/ReadAll with the mixed-depth partition walk that matches on filename suffix so one pass covers both dt=*/system=*/ and legacy dt=*/ layouts.

(b) Two S3 adapters duplicating AWS SDK plumbing:

    internal/cachestore/s3store/s3store.go     81 lines
    internal/ndjsonstore/s3ndjson/s3ndjson.go  92 lines

Both wrap config.LoadDefaultConfig in a New(ctx, bucket, prefix), both define a private api interface subsetting the S3 client, both build near-identical PutObjectInput / GetObjectInput with a prefix-joined key. They differ only in error mapping (NoSuchKey -> found=false vs a plain error), key suffixing (.json vs raw), and which extra operation they need (DeleteObject vs ListObjectsV2).

EXPLICITLY NOT DUPLICATION -- do not "fix" this: the two Store INTERFACES are genuinely different shapes and should stay different.

    cache.Store       Get(key) ([]byte, bool, error) · Put · Remove      -- keyed TTL cache: delete-capable, no enumeration
    ndjsonstore.Store Get(key) ([]byte, error) · Put · List(prefix)      -- append-only partitioned log: enumerable, no delete

Those signatures reflect real semantic differences between the Cache and the durable stores. Only the SDK plumbing beneath them is shared.

Surfaced by the 2026-07-22 architecture review (candidate 7 of 7, rated Speculative).
design:
Two independently shippable halves; either can be done without the other, and either can be declined.

(a) Drop the wrapper constructors. Keep GradeRow / Row, ObjectKey, SystemFromKey, LegacySystem, MarshalNDJSON and the decorate hook in their domain packages. Callers (cmd/grade.go, cmd/team-values.go, cmd/projection-site.go) hold an ndjsonstore.Store and call the package-level functions. Note this interacts with the State Store issue (rosterbot-9s6): if statestore returns a byte-level store, these call sites become a one-liner and the wrappers have even less to justify them. Sequence after 9s6 rather than before.

(b) Share one s3blob adapter under the two Store shapes: a common Put/Get/List/Delete over the AWS SDK, plus a thin shim per Store interface handling the not-found mapping and key suffixing. Roughly 100 of 173 lines collapse.

Caveat on (a): the wrappers are what currently make analysis and teamvalue reach ~94% and 100% coverage with in-memory stores. Removing them must not push that coverage onto untested cmd/ code -- if the wrappers are the reason the domain packages are well tested, keeping them is a defensible answer and this half should be declined.
acceptance_criteria:
Either half may be closed as declined with reasoning; not all of this needs doing.

If (a) is done:
  1. The eight pass-through constructors across analysis and teamvalue are gone; row types, ObjectKey, SystemFromKey, LegacySystem and the decorate hook remain in their domain packages.
  2. Coverage for internal/analysis and internal/teamvalue does not regress, and the logic does not migrate into untested cmd/ code.
  3. Legacy partition reads (dt=X/grades.ndjson with no system= segment, attributed to analysis.LegacySystem) still work -- verified against the projection dashboard.

If (b) is done:
  4. One S3 blob adapter backs both Store shapes; per-Store shims handle not-found mapping and key suffixing only.
  5. The AWS SDK stays out of internal/cache and internal/ndjsonstore leaves.
  6. ADR-0002 is amended to reflect a shared adapter, rather than being silently contradicted (it currently asks for an isolated S3 adapter per store).

Always:
  7. The two Store interfaces remain distinct shapes -- this issue must not unify cache.Store and ndjsonstore.Store.
  8. go vet ./... , make build-modules and make test pass; a real S3 read/write path is exercised at least once before merge.
close_reason: Half (b) shipped in PR #90 (fe3fa2c), merged to main: one shared internal/s3blob Blob under all ten S3-backed stores, per-store shims own only key layout + not-found policy, AWS SDK stays out of the internal/cache and internal/ndjsonstore leaves, the two Store shapes remain distinct (criterion 7 held), and ADR-0002 amended at docs/adr/0002:75-89 to say 'isolated Store shape, not an isolated copy of the SDK plumbing' (criterion 6). Half (a) DECLINED per this issue's own acceptance criteria ('either half may be closed as declined'): the eight pass-through constructors in internal/analysis and internal/teamvalue remain (analysis/grades.go:86, teamvalue/teamvalue.go:101). They are the documented seam cmd/ wires stores through and were the lowest-payoff item of the seven from the 2026-07-22 review; deleting them would push construction into untested cmd/ code, against criterion 2. Refile if that changes.

title: Drop redundant manual Go tarball install from buildspec.yml
description: Follow-up from rosterbot-2no. buildspec.yml's install phase still curls+untars Go ${GO_VERSION} (1.25.0) to /usr/local/go and prepends it to PATH, but the post-merge build 0e2b8e1a on the new AL2023-based image logged 'go version go1.26.1' at the very command that follows the PATH export -- i.e. the image's own golang runtime is doing the build, and the manual 1.25.0 install is shadowed dead weight (~5s wasted per build, and it's silently not the toolchain that actually builds infra/). infra/go.mod requires Go 1.25; the image's go1.26.1 satisfies that and cdk deploy (go run infra.go) succeeded on it. Fix: delete GO_VERSION + the curl/rm/tar/export-PATH lines (install phase AND the duplicate export in post_build), add 'golang: 1.25' (or 1.26) to phases.install.runtime-versions. This is the 'Also switch Go to the image runtime' option deferred during rosterbot-2no; now has live evidence it works. Verify via a post-merge build on main (host image behavior not testable locally).
acceptance_criteria: buildspec.yml no longer manually downloads Go; golang runtime selected via runtime-versions; a post-merge build succeeds (go build/vet of infra, cdk deploy, docker build/push) with the image-provided Go.
close_reason: Shipped in ace9e96. buildspec.yml now selects Go via runtime-versions (golang: 1.26) instead of curl+untar of 1.25.0. Post-merge CodeBuild 86536e5c on ace9e96 SUCCEEDED end-to-end: INSTALL 2s (logged 'go version go1.26.1 linux/arm64', no toolchain auto-download), BUILD (docker) + POST_BUILD (cdk deploy incl. host-Go lambda/buildnotify bundling, dashboard publish, projection-site) all green. Chose 1.26 over infra's 1.25 floor so host go satisfies the 1.26.1 lambda modules bundled by cdk deploy.

title: Bump CodeBuild image off EOL Node 18 (cdk CLI deprecation warning)
description:
The CodeBuild project's build-host image (awscodebuild.LinuxArmBuildImage_AMAZON_LINUX_2_STANDARD_3_0(), infra/infra.go ~line 304) ships Node 18.20.8, which the aws-cdk npm CLI now flags as EOL on every 'install' phase run (banner warning in build logs as of the 2026-07-17 build of PR #63/commit 0302977). Not currently build-breaking -- cdk still runs -- just noisy.

Fix: bump BuildImage to a newer AL2/AL2023 standard image version that bundles a supported Node LTS (or add an explicit phases.install.runtime-versions.nodejs override if the current image supports it). Verify via an actual CodeBuild run on main (this project's build only triggers on push to main, and build-host image behavior can't be tested locally) -- confirm Go download/toolchain, npm install -g aws-cdk, and docker build/push all still work under the new image before merging.
acceptance_criteria: CodeBuild install phase no longer prints a Node EOL warning, and a full post-merge build (image push, cdk deploy, dashboard publish, projection-site render) succeeds under the new build image.
notes: VERIFIED on post-merge build 0e2b8e1a (SUCCEEDED, 2026-07-21 ~22:35 UTC, source b021141). Install-phase log shows: 'Selecting nodejs runtime version 22 based on manual selections' -> node/22.22.1 installed; cdk 2.1128.1 ran with ZERO Node EOL/deprecation banner (grep of all 401 head lines for end-of-life/NodeDeprecation/NodeVersionSupport/v18 = no matches; baseline build 8f1ce0f3 had 4 such lines). Build went green end-to-end (SUCCEEDED => all post_build cmds exit 0: docker push, cdk deploy, dashboard s3 sync + CF invalidation, projection-site run-task). Project env.image now = aws/codebuild/amazonlinux-aarch64-standard:3.0 (AL2023), applied by this build's own cdk deploy. NOTE: the runtime-versions:nodejs:22 pin is what removed the banner -- it took effect immediately even though this build's env.image was still the old amazonlinux2-aarch64-standard:3.0 tag (that :3.0 tag is itself AL2023-based and honors runtime-versions). The image bump is correct hygiene but was not strictly required for the Node fix. Follow-up: go version reported go1.26.1 (image runtime), NOT the manually-installed 1.25.0 tarball -> manual Go install is shadowed/dead weight; filed as follow-up bead.

title: Share HKB player-enrichment lookup between claims and transactions
description: internal/claims/hkb.go (lookupHKB, building a SidePlayer) and internal/transactions/transactions.go (the TradePlayer builder) independently map an hkb.Player record onto a near-identical enriched struct -- Rank, Value, Trend30D/ValueChange30D, Level, Prospect, IsPitcher, ERA/WHIP or OPS depending on pitcher-vs-hitter -- both keyed by playername.Normalize(name) lookup into a map built from internal/hkb data. transactions.go even has a normalizeName wrapper that just calls playername.Normalize directly. Architecture review (improve-codebase-architecture, 2026-07-12) flagged this as real duplication by the deletion test: deleting either lookup function would force the other package to reproduce the same field-by-field mapping.
design: Move the enrichment mapping into internal/hkb (already the leaf package that owns HKB data) as a shared function, e.g. hkb.Enrich(name, position string, lookup map[string]hkb.Player) returning a shared enriched-player value. internal/claims and internal/transactions both call it instead of maintaining their own copy; their SidePlayer/TradePlayer types either become thin aliases of the shared shape or embed it.
acceptance_criteria: One enrichment function lives in internal/hkb. internal/claims/hkb.go and internal/transactions/transactions.go both call it; the duplicated field-mapping logic is deleted from at least one of the two packages. Existing claims and transactions tests pass unchanged.
notes: Filed from improve-codebase-architecture review, 2026-07-12. Lowest priority of the four candidates from that review -- small, mechanical, low risk.
close_reason: Moved HKB enrichment mapping into internal/hkb.Enrich/BuildLookup, shared by claims and transactions

title: CYC/NH/PG bonus stats unhandled in MLB game-log backfill scorer
description: CYC (cycle) is a declared league scoring category but is absent from ApplyHitter's statMap (internal/scoring/hitter.go:36-42); NH (no-hitter) and PG (perfect game, listed at 25/75 pts in strategist's review) are similarly absent from ApplyPitcher. Correctly omitted from projections (unprojectable event-level bonuses), and self-cancels in grading since both projected and actual sides omit them equally. The only real gap is internal/fantrax/mlb_backfill.go's single-game log scorer (used by recap/backtest for a waiver pickup's first-day FPts), which COULD detect these from one game's box line (cycle = >=1 each of 1B/2B/3B/HR in a game; no-hitter/perfect game from H/BB/HBP/ER over 9 IP) but currently doesn't, so a backfilled day containing one of these events under-counts FPts by the bonus amount.
acceptance_criteria: Add cycle/no-hitter/perfect-game detection to the mlb_backfill.go single-game scorer so historical grading is exact. Confirm the league's actual Fantrax CYC/NH/PG weights first (bd notes both agents flagged this independently but neither confirmed the live weight value).
notes: From both fantasy-baseball-model-auditor (L1) and fantasy-baseball-strategist (finding #5) reviews, 2026-07-10. Very low real-world frequency (~2-3 cycles/year leaguewide); lowest priority of this review's findings.

comments.author: Jon Nixon
comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Rare in-game bonus events (a batter hitting for the cycle, a pitcher throwing a no-hitter or perfect game) aren't detected when reconstructing a player's historical single-day fantasy point total from raw box-score-style game logs, undercounting that day's points by the bonus amount whenever one of these rare events occurs.

**Current behavior:**
The league's scoring rules include bonus point values for these three rare single-game achievements. The regular projection and live-scoring paths correctly don't attempt to project them (they're unprojectable rare events). But the historical single-game reconstruction path — used to backfill a day's fantasy points from raw stats when needed (e.g. for a player's first day after a waiver pickup) — also doesn't check for them, even though it has access to the full single-game stat line needed to detect all three.

**Desired behavior:**
The historical single-game reconstruction path should detect all three events from the game's stat line and add the corresponding bonus points, so historical point totals are exactly correct even on the rare day one of these occurs.

**Key interfaces:**
- The single-game stat-line-to-points scorer used by the historical backfill path.
- Cycle detection needs at least one single, double, triple, and home run in the same game.
- No-hitter/perfect-game detection needs innings-pitched, hits-allowed, walks-allowed, and hit-by-pitch-allowed (perfect game additionally requires zero baserunners by any means) over a minimum of 9 innings.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Before implementing, confirm the league's actual configured point values for these three categories (they may already be zero, in which case this is a no-op and the issue should just be closed with that finding).
- [ ] If non-zero, a synthetic game line representing each of the three events is correctly detected and scores the bonus.
- [ ] A normal game log with none of these events is unaffected.

**Out of scope:**
- Adding these to the season-long or per-game projection paths (they remain intentionally unprojectable) — only the historical single-game backfill/reconstruction path is in scope.
